A right-angled triangle has an angle of 60° at the top vertex. The side next to that angle is 4 cm and the hypotenuse from it is x cm.

Given that cos 60° = 0.5, work out the value of x.
answer: 8 — cos 60° is adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, so 0.5 = 4⁄x
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
The times that 48 trains left a station on Monday were recorded. A cumulative frequency graph gives information about the numbers of minutes the trains were delayed, correct to the nearest minute. Reading off it, 12 trains were delayed 4 minutes or less, 24 were delayed 10 minutes or less and 36 were delayed 20 minutes or less.

The shortest delay was 0 minutes and the longest delay was 42 minutes.

On the grid below, draw a box plot for the information about the delays on Monday.
answer: Whiskers at 0 and 42, box from 4 to 20, median line at 10 — with 48 trains the quartiles are the 12th, 24th and 36th values, read off the curve. The curve finishing at 48 confirms the scale.
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
48 trains left the station on Tuesday. A box plot for Tuesday has whiskers at 0 and 33, a box from 6 to 17 and a median at 9.

Compare the distribution of the delays on Monday with the distribution of the delays on Tuesday.
answer: The median delay was longer on Monday (10 minutes against 9), so trains were typically delayed a little more. And Monday’s interquartile range is 20 − 4 = 16 minutes against Tuesday’s 17 − 6 = 11, so Monday’s delays were more spread out.
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Mary says, “The longest delay on Tuesday was 33 minutes. This means that there must be some delays of between 25 minutes and 30 minutes.”

Is Mary right? You must give a reason for your answer.
answer: No. A box plot only marks the smallest value, the quartiles and the largest value — it says nothing about where the values in between fall, so there could be no delays at all between 25 and 30 minutes.
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018

html: Simplify (x − 1)⁄5(x − 1)2
answer: 1⁄5(x − 1) — one factor of (x − 1) cancels

subject: Maths

html: Factorise fully 50 − 2y2
answer: 2(5 + y)(5 − y) — take out the 2 first, then 25 − y2 is the difference of two squares
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Jack’s idea for a special offer is to put 25% more cereal into each box and not change the price. Sadia’s idea is to reduce the price and not change the amount of cereal in each box.

Sadia wants her idea to give the same value for money as Jack’s idea. By what percentage does she need to reduce the price?
answer: 20% — take a box costing £1 holding 100 g. Jack sells 125 g for £1, which is 0.8p per gram. For Sadia to match that on 100 g she must charge 80p
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
A, B and C are points on the circumference of a circle, centre O. DAE is the tangent to the circle at A. Angle BAE = 56° and angle CBO = 35°

Work out the size of angle CAO. You must show all your working.
answer: 21° — by the alternate segment theorem the tangent-chord angle BAE equals the angle in the alternate segment, so angle ACB = 56°. OB = OC are radii, so triangle OBC is isosceles and angle OCB = 35°, which leaves angle ACO = 56 − 35 = 21°. OA = OC are radii too, so triangle OAC is isosceles and angle CAO = angle ACO
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Triangle A has vertices (−4, −1), (−4, −4) and (2, −4). Triangle B has vertices (2, 4), (4, 4) and (4, 3).

Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
answer: An enlargement of scale factor −1⁄3, centre (2, 2) — B is a third the size of A and turned through half a turn. All three vertices check: (−4, −4) → (4, 4), (−4, −1) → (4, 3) and (2, −4) → (2, 4)
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018

accept: An enlargement of scale factor −1⁄3, centre (2, 2)

html: Work out the value of (16⁄81)3⁄4
answer: <sup>8</sup>⁄<sub>27</sub> — the fourth root of <sup>16</sup>⁄<sub>81</sub> is <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>, and cubing it gives <sup>8</sup>⁄<sub>27</sub>
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
3a = 1⁄9, 3b = 9√3 and 3c = 1⁄√3

Work out the value of a + b + c
answer: 0 — writing each as a power of 3: a = −2, b = 2.5 (since 9√3 = 32 × 3½) and c = −0.5. They cancel exactly.
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Three solid shapes A, B and C are similar. The surface area of shape A is 4 cm2 and the surface area of shape B is 25 cm2. The ratio of the volume of shape B to the volume of shape C is 27 : 64

Work out the ratio of the height of shape A to the height of shape C. Give your answer in its simplest form.
answer: 3 : 10 — areas scale by the square of the lengths, so A : B is √4 : √25 = 2 : 5. Volumes scale by the cube, so B : C is ∛27 : ∛64 = 3 : 4. Matching B in both gives 6 : 15 and 15 : 20, so A : C is 6 : 20
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: Prove algebraically that 0.2̇5̇6̇ — that is 0.2565656…, with the 5 and the 6 recurring — can be written as 127⁄495
answer: Let x = 0.2565656…. Then 100x = 25.6565656…, and the recurring tails are identical, so subtracting gives 99x = 25.4. Hence x = 25.4⁄99 = 254⁄990, and dividing top and bottom by 2 gives 127⁄495
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
The equation of a curve is y = x2 + ax + b where a and b are integers. The points (0, −5) and (5, 0) lie on the curve.

Find the coordinates of the turning point of the curve.
answer: (2, −9) — (0, −5) gives b = −5, and (5, 0) gives 25 + 5a − 5 = 0, so a = −4. Completing the square, y = (x − 2)2 − 9. The roots would then be 5 and −1, which is what the sketch shows.
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
The graph of y = f(x) is a parabola through (0, 0) and (2, 0) with its lowest point at (1, −1).

On the grid above, sketch the graph of y = f(x − 2)
answer: The same curve moved 2 to the right: through (2, 0) and (4, 0) with its lowest point at (3, −1)
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
On a grid, graph A has been reflected to give graph B; the two are mirror images in the y-axis. The equation of graph A is y = g(x)

Write down the equation of graph B.
answer: y = g(−x) — a reflection in the y-axis replaces x by −x
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
For all values of x, f(x) = (x + 1)2 and g(x) = 2(x − 1)

Show that gf(x) = 2x(x + 2)
answer: gf(x) means g of (x + 1)2, which is 2((x + 1)2 − 1). Expanding, (x + 1)2 − 1 = x2 + 2x + 1 − 1 = x2 + 2x, so gf(x) = 2(x2 + 2x) = 2x(x + 2)
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: Find g−1(7)
answer: 4.5 — g−1(7) is the number g sends to 7, so solve 2(x − 1) = 7
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: Show that (√18 + √2)2⁄(√8 − 2) can be written in the form a(b + √2) where a and b are integers.
answer: 16(1 + √2), so a = 16 and b = 1 — on top, √18 = 3√2, so the bracket is 4√2 and its square is 32. Underneath, √8 = 2√2, so the denominator is 2(√2 − 1) and the fraction is 16⁄(√2 − 1). Multiplying top and bottom by (√2 + 1) makes the denominator 2 − 1 = 1, leaving 16(√2 + 1). It checks numerically: both sides are 38.627…
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
OAB is a triangle. OPM and APN are straight lines and M is the midpoint of AB. OA = a, OB = b and OP : PM = 3 : 2

Work out the ratio ON : NB
answer: 3 : 4 — OM = ½(a + b), so OP = 3⁄5 of that = 3⁄10(a + b). Then AP = OP − a = −7⁄10a + 3⁄10b. N is on OB, so ON = kb and AN = kb − a. For A, P and N to be in a straight line these must be multiples of each other: matching the a parts gives the multiplier 10⁄7, and then k = 3⁄7. So ON is 3⁄7 of OB and NB is 4⁄7
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
There are only green pens and blue pens in a box. There are three more blue pens than green pens in the box, and there are more than 12 pens in the box.

Simon is going to take at random two pens from the box. The probability that Simon will take two pens of the same colour is 27⁄55

Work out the number of green pens in the box.
answer: 21 — with g green and g + 3 blue in a box of 2g + 3, the chance of a matching pair is [g(g − 1) + (g + 3)(g + 2)] ÷ [(2g + 3)(2g + 2)] = 27⁄55. That has exactly two whole-number solutions, g = 4 (a box of 11) and g = 21 (a box of 45) — which is what the “more than 12 pens” condition is there to settle.
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
ℰ = {even numbers between 1 and 25}, A = {2, 8, 10, 14}, B = {6, 8, 20} and C = {8, 18, 20, 22}

Complete the Venn diagram for this information.
answer: 8 goes in the middle, where all three overlap. 20 goes in B ∩ C only; nothing else is in two sets at once. 2, 10 and 14 go in A alone, 6 in B alone, 18 and 22 in C alone, and 4, 12, 16, 24 sit outside all three circles. That is 12 numbers in all, which is how many even numbers there are between 1 and 25.
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: A number is chosen at random from ℰ. Find the probability that the number is a member of A ∩ B.
answer: 1⁄12 — A ∩ B is just {8}, and there are 12 numbers in ℰ
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Sean has information about the height, in cm, and the weight, in kg, of each of ten rugby players. He is asked to draw a scatter graph and a line of best fit. He plots the points accurately on axes whose horizontal scale runs 140, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200 at equal spacings, and draws a line rising from (140, 85) to (200, 105) with nine of the ten points below it.

Write down two things that are wrong with his answer.
answer: First, the scale on the height axis is not even — the gap from 140 to 160 is 20 cm but every other gap is 10 cm, so the points are plotted in the wrong places along it. Second, the line of best fit does not fit: almost every point lies below it, and it runs well past the data at the left-hand end where there are no players at all.
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
BEG is a triangle. ABC and DEF are parallel lines, with B on the upper line and E on the lower one. Angle DEB = 110°, angle GBC = 35° and angle GEF = 25°. Angle x is the angle BGE.

Work out the size of angle x. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
answer: 60° — angle BEF = 180 − 110 = 70° (angles on a straight line), so angle ABE = 70° (alternate angles between the parallel lines). Then angle EBG = 180 − 70 − 35 = 75° (angles on the straight line ABC), and angle BEG = 180 − 110 − 25 = 45° (angles on the straight line DEF). The angles of triangle BEG add to 180°, so x = 180 − 75 − 45
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
A bank has two accounts, both paying compound interest: a cash savings account at 2.5% per annum and a shares account at 3.5% per annum. Ali invests £2000 in the cash savings account and Ben invests £1600 in the shares account.

Work out who will get the most interest by the end of 3 years. You must show all your working.
answer: Ben. Ali has 2000 × 1.025<sup>3</sup> = £2153.78, so £153.78 of interest. Ben has 1600 × 1.035<sup>3</sup> = £1773.95, so £173.95 — about £20 more, even though he invested £400 less.
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: In the 3rd year the rate of interest for the shares account is changed to 4% per annum. Does this affect who will get the most interest by the end of 3 years? Give a reason for your answer.
answer: No. Ben was already getting more interest, and raising his rate only increases it further — to £182.52. Ali’s account is untouched, so Ben still gets the most.
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
A floor is a trapezium with parallel sides 10 m and 16 m that are 7 m apart. John is going to paint the floor. Each 5 litre tin of paint costs £16.99 and 1 litre of paint covers an area of 2 m2. John has £160 to spend on paint.

Has John got enough money to buy all the paint he needs? You must show how you get your answer.
answer: No. The floor is ½ × (10 + 16) × 7 = 91 m<sup>2</sup>, which needs 91 ÷ 2 = 45.5 litres. Paint comes in 5 litre tins, and 45.5 ÷ 5 = 9.1, so he must buy 10 tins — you cannot buy nine-tenths of a tin. That costs 10 × 16.99 = £169.90, which is £9.90 more than he has.
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
A is the point with coordinates (5, 9) and B is the point with coordinates (d, 15). The gradient of the line AB is 3

Work out the value of d.
answer: d = 7 — the rise from 9 to 15 is 6, and gradient 3 means the run is 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so d = 5 + 2
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: Write the number 0.000 086 23 in standard form.
answer: 8.623 × 10<sup>−5</sup>
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Work out (3.2 × 103 + 5.1 × 10−2)⁄(4.3 × 10−4)

Give your answer in standard form, correct to 3 significant figures.
answer: 7.44 × 10<sup>6</sup> — the top comes to 3200.051 and dividing by 0.00043 gives 7 441 979…
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Triangle P has vertices (−1, 3), (3, 3) and (3, 5). Triangle P is reflected in the line y = −x to give triangle Q. Triangle Q is reflected in the line x = −1 to give triangle R.

Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle R to triangle P.
answer: A rotation of 90° anticlockwise about (−1, 1). Following P through: the first reflection sends (−1, 3), (3, 3), (3, 5) to (−3, 1), (−3, −3), (−5, −3), and the second sends those to (1, 1), (1, −3), (3, −3), which is R. All three of those rotate back onto P about (−1, 1), the point where the two mirror lines cross — two reflections in lines meeting at 45° always make a 90° turn about that point.
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Martin truncates the number N to 1 digit. The result is 7

Write down the error interval for N.
answer: 7 ≤ N < 8 — truncating throws away everything after the first digit rather than rounding, so anything from 7 up to (but not including) 8 truncates to 7. Note this is not the rounding interval 6.5 to 7.5
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
Robert makes 50 litres of green paint by mixing yellow paint and blue paint in the ratio 2 : 3. Yellow paint is sold in 5 litre tins costing £26 each. Blue paint is sold in 10 litre tins costing £48 each. Robert sells all the green paint he makes in 10 litre tins, at £66.96 for each tin.

Work out Robert’s percentage profit on each tin of green paint he sells.
answer: 35% — the mix is 20 litres of yellow (four 5 litre tins, £104) and 30 litres of blue (three 10 litre tins, £144), so 50 litres costs £248. He sells five 10 litre tins for £334.80, a profit of £86.80, and 86.80 ÷ 248 = 0.35 exactly
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html:
In a restaurant there are 9 starter dishes, 15 main dishes and 8 dessert dishes. Janet is going to choose either a starter and a main, or a main and a dessert, or a starter, a main and a dessert.

Show that there are 1335 different ways to choose the meal.
answer: A starter and a main is 9 × 15 = 135 ways. A main and a dessert is 15 × 8 = 120. All three courses is 9 × 15 × 8 = 1080. The three choices cannot happen together, so they add: 135 + 120 + 1080 = 1335
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018
subject: Maths

html: Write (4x2 − 9)⁄(6x + 9) × 2x⁄(x2 − 3x) in the form (ax + b)⁄(cx + d) where a, b, c and d are integers.
answer: (4x − 6)⁄(3x − 9) — factorise everything: 4x2 − 9 = (2x − 3)(2x + 3), 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3) and x2 − 3x = x(x − 3). The (2x + 3) and the x cancel, leaving 2(2x − 3) over 3(x − 3)
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2018

html: Express 3⁄(x + 1) + 1⁄(x − 2) − 4⁄x as a single fraction in its simplest form.

What is the probability that Joe and Mary take counters of different colours?

html:
p and q are two numbers such that p > q. When you subtract 5 from p and subtract 5 from q the answers are in the ratio 5 : 1. When you add 20 to p and add 20 to q the answers are in the ratio 5 : 2.

Find the ratio p : q. Give your answer in its simplest form.
answer: 4 : 1 — the first ratio gives p − 5 = 5(q − 5), so p = 5q − 20. The second gives 2(p + 20) = 5(q + 20), so 2p = 5q + 60. Substituting, 10q − 40 = 5q + 60, so q = 20 and p = 80. Both conditions check: 75 : 15 is 5 : 1 and 100 : 40 is 5 : 2

html:
A frustum is made by removing a cone of height 3.2 cm from a solid cone of height 6.4 cm and base diameter 7.2 cm. The frustum is joined to a solid hemisphere of diameter 7.2 cm to form a solid S. The volume of a sphere is 4⁄3πr3 and the volume of a cone is 1⁄3πr2h.

The density of the frustum is 2.4 g/cm3 and the density of the hemisphere is 4.8 g/cm3. Calculate the average density of solid S.
answer: 3.75 g/cm<sup>3</sup> — the removed cone is half the height, so its radius is half too: 1.8 cm. The frustum is <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>π × 3.6<sup>2</sup> × 6.4 − <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>π × 1.8<sup>2</sup> × 3.2 = 76.00… cm<sup>3</sup> and the hemisphere is <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub>π × 3.6<sup>3</sup> = 97.72… cm<sup>3</sup>. The masses are 182.40 g and 469.04 g, so the average density is 651.44 ÷ 173.72, which comes out at exactly 3.75. Note it is total mass ÷ total volume, not the average of 2.4 and 4.8

html:
A, B, R and P are four points on a circle with centre O. A, O, R and C are four points on a different circle. The two circles intersect at the points A and R. CPA, CRB and AOB are straight lines.

Prove that angle CAB = angle ABC.
answer: AOB is a straight line through the centre O, so AB is a diameter of the first circle and angle ARB = 90° (the angle in a semicircle). CRB is a straight line, so angle ARC = 180 − 90 = 90° (angles on a straight line). Now A, O, R and C lie on the second circle and angle ARC is 90°, so AC must be a diameter of that circle (the converse of the angle in a semicircle). O is on that circle too, so angle AOC = 90° for the same reason. That makes CO perpendicular to AB, and O is the midpoint of AB because it is the centre of the first circle — so CO is the perpendicular bisector of AB and CA = CB. Triangle CAB is therefore isosceles, and angle CAB = angle ABC (base angles of an isosceles triangle).

html:
White shapes and black shapes are used in a game. Some are circles and all the others are squares. The ratio of white shapes to black shapes is 3 : 7. The ratio of white circles to white squares is 4 : 5. The ratio of black circles to black squares is 2 : 5.

Work out what fraction of all the shapes are circles.
answer: <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> — the white shapes split into 9 parts and the black into 7, so scale the 3 : 7 up to 27 : 63 to make both splits whole. Then the white circles are <sup>4</sup>⁄<sub>9</sub> of 27 = 12 and the black circles <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>7</sub> of 63 = 18, giving 30 circles out of 90 shapes

html:
A cone has a volume of 98 cm3 and a radius of 5.13 cm. The volume of a cone is 1⁄3πr2h.

Work out an estimate for the height of the cone.
answer: 4 cm — round everything to 1 significant figure: volume 100, radius 5, π as 3. Then 100 = 1⁄3 × 3 × 25 × h, so h = 4. It is an estimate, so the mark scheme takes anything from 3.5 to 4.5 — what is being marked is rounding first and then rearranging, not the figure

subject: Maths

html: John uses a calculator to work out the height of the cone to 2 decimal places. Will your estimate be more than John’s answer or less than John’s answer? Give reasons for your answer.
answer: More. All three roundings push the answer the same way: the volume was rounded UP (98 to 100), which makes the height bigger, while the radius and π were both rounded DOWN (5.13 to 5, 3.14… to 3), which makes the bottom of the fraction smaller and the height bigger again. John’s answer is 3.56 cm against the estimate of 4

html: n is an integer greater than 1. Prove algebraically that n2 − 2 − (n − 2)2 is always an even number.
answer: Expand the bracket: (n − 2)2 = n2 − 4n + 4. So the expression is n2 − 2 − n2 + 4n − 4 = 4n − 6. That is 2(2n − 3), which is 2 times a whole number and therefore even for every integer n.

html:
There are 9 counters in a bag. 7 of the counters are green and 2 of the counters are blue. Ria takes at random two counters from the bag.

Work out the probability that Ria takes one counter of each colour. You must show your working.
answer: <sup>7</sup>⁄<sub>18</sub> — the counters are not replaced, so the second denominator is 8. Green then blue is <sup>7</sup>⁄<sub>9</sub> × <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> and blue then green is <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>9</sub> × <sup>7</sup>⁄<sub>8</sub> — the same product, so double it: <sup>28</sup>⁄<sub>72</sub>

And BC = CB, the side both triangles share. Two sides and the angle between them match, so the triangles are congruent (SAS). html:
A hexagon ABCDEF is made of two congruent parallelograms ABEF and CBED where AB = BC = x cm. P is the point on AF and Q is the point on CD such that BP = BQ = 10 cm.

Given that angle ABC = 30°, prove that cos PBQ = 1 − ((2 − √3)⁄200)x2
answer:
First, PQ = AC. AF and CD are both parallel to BE because each is a side of one of the parallelograms, so AP is parallel to CQ; and the parallelograms are congruent with BP = BQ, so AP = CQ. A quadrilateral with one pair of sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram, so APQC is one and PQ = AC.
Now the cosine rule twice. In triangle ABC, with AB = BC = x and the angle between them 30°: AC2 = x2 + x2 − 2x2cos 30° = 2x2 − √3x2 = (2 − √3)x2, since cos 30° = √3⁄2.
In triangle PBQ, with BP = BQ = 10: PQ2 = 100 + 100 − 200 cos PBQ. Setting the two equal, because PQ = AC: (2 − √3)x2 = 200 − 200 cos PBQ. Rearranging gives cos PBQ = 1 − ((2 − √3)⁄200)x2

A table shows the probabilities that a biased dice will land on 2, on 3, on 4, on 5 and on 6: they are 0.17, 0.18, 0.09, 0.15 and 0.1. The probability of landing on 1 is left blank.

Neymar rolls the biased dice 200 times. Work out an estimate for the total number of times the dice will land on 1 or on 3

html:
On Saturday, some adults and some children were in a theatre. The ratio of adults to children was 5 : 2. Each person had a seat in the Circle or in the Stalls. 3⁄4 of the children had seats in the Stalls and 117 children had seats in the Circle. There are exactly 2600 seats in the theatre.

On this Saturday, were there people on more than 60% of the seats? You must show how you get your answer.
answer: Yes. The 117 children in the Circle are the quarter not in the Stalls, so there were 468 children, and the 5 : 2 ratio makes that 1170 adults. That is 1638 people in 2600 seats, which is exactly 63% — above 60%.

A prism has a cross section in the shape of a trapezium, with dimensions 2 m, 2 m, 1 m, 0.5 m, 0.5 m and a length of 2.5 m.

On the centimetre grid below, draw the front elevation and the side elevation of the prism. Use a scale of 2 cm to 1 m.
answer: At 2 cm to the metre every length doubles on the page: the front elevation is the trapezium cross section drawn 4 cm and 2 cm across its parallel sides and 1 cm tall, and the side elevation is a 5 cm by 1 cm rectangle, because a prism seen from the side is its length by its height.

html:
Olly drove 56 km from Liverpool to Manchester and then 61 km from Manchester to Sheffield. His average speed from Liverpool to Manchester was 70 km/h, and he took 75 minutes to drive from Manchester to Sheffield.

Work out Olly’s average speed for his total drive from Liverpool to Sheffield.
answer: 57.1 km/h — the first leg took 56 ÷ 70 = 0.8 hours, which is 48 minutes, so the whole drive was 117 km in 123 minutes = 2.05 hours. Average speed is total distance ÷ total time, not the mean of the two speeds: 117 ÷ 2.05 = 57.07…

html:
Janie drove from Barnsley to York. Her average speed from Barnsley to Leeds was 80 km/h and from Leeds to York was 60 km/h. Janie says that the average speed from Barnsley to York can be found by working out the mean of 80 km/h and 60 km/h.

If Janie is correct, what does this tell you about the two parts of Janie’s journey?
answer: The two parts took the same amount of TIME. Averaging the speeds only works when each speed is held for equally long — which means the faster leg covered more distance.

ABC and EDC are straight lines and EA is parallel to DB. EC = 8.1 cm, DC = 5.4 cm and DB = 2.6 cm.

Work out the length of AE.

html:
Anil wants to invest £25 000 for 3 years. Personal Bank pays compound interest of 2% for each year. Secure Bank pays compound interest of 4.3% for the first year and 0.9% for each extra year.

Which bank will give Anil the most interest at the end of 3 years? You must show all your working.
answer: Secure Bank. Personal Bank gives 25 000 × 1.02<sup>3</sup> = £26 530.20, so £1530.20 of interest. Secure Bank gives 25 000 × 1.043 × 1.009<sup>2</sup> = £26 546.46, so £1546.46 — about £16 more

A number, n, is rounded to 2 decimal places. The result is 4.76

Using inequalities, write down the error interval for n.
answer: 4.755 ≤ n < 4.765 — anything from halfway below to halfway above rounds to 4.76, and the upper end is strict because 4.765 itself rounds up to 4.77

A cumulative frequency graph shows the heights, in cm, of 60 students. Reading off it, 48 of the students are 160 cm or shorter.

Work out an estimate for the number of these students with a height greater than 160 cm.

html:
Kyle reflects triangle A in the x-axis to get triangle B, then reflects B in the line y = x to get triangle C. Amy reflects triangle A in the line y = x to get triangle D, then reflects D in the x-axis to get triangle E.

Amy says that triangle E should be in the same position as triangle C. Is Amy correct? You must show how you get your answer.
answer: No. Follow a point (x, y) through each route. Kyle: reflecting in the x-axis gives (x, −y), and then reflecting in y = x swaps the coordinates to (−y, x). Amy: reflecting in y = x first gives (y, x), and then the x-axis gives (y, −x). Those are not the same point — they are a half turn apart — so the order of two reflections matters.

Write down the name of the planet with the greatest mass.

Is Mr Slater right? Give a reason for your answer.
answer: No. For both events to happen you MULTIPLY: 0.4 × 0.25 = 0.1. Adding is for one event OR another, and his 0.65 is larger than either probability on its own, which cannot be right for “both”.

html:
A histogram shows the ages of the 134 members of a sports club. The frequency densities are 1.1 for 0–10, 2.8 for 10–20, 2.3 for 20–40, 1.4 for 40–60 and 0.7 for 60–90 years.

20% of the members of the sports club who are over 50 years of age are female. Work out an estimate for the number of female members who are over 50 years of age.
answer: 7 — frequency is density × class width, giving 11, 28, 46, 28 and 21 members. Those add to 134, which is the membership the question states, so the bars have been read correctly. Over 50 means half of the 40–60 bar (1.4 × 10 = 14) plus all of the 60–90 bar (21), which is 35, and 20% of 35 = 7 exactly

html: Nine sketch graphs are labelled A to I. Match each of y = sin x, y = x3 + 4x, y = 2x and y = 4⁄x with the letter of its graph.

answer: Angle BAE = angle CDE, because angles in the same segment are equal — both stand on the arc BC. Angle ABE = angle DCE for the same reason, both standing on the arc AD. And angle AEB = angle DEC because they are vertically opposite. All three angles match, so the triangles are similar (AAA).

Three identical circles sit inside a rectangle, two side by side along the top and one below between them. Each circle touches the other two circles and the sides of the rectangle. The radius of each circle is 24 mm.

Work out the area of the rectangle. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
answer: 8600 mm<sup>2</sup> — the width is four radii, 96 mm, because the two top circles sit side by side against the two vertical sides. For the height, the three centres form an equilateral triangle of side 48 (two radii), whose height is 24√3. Adding a radius at the top and a radius at the bottom gives 48 + 24√3 = 89.569… mm, so the area is 96 × 89.569… = 8598.6…
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Here are the first five terms of a sequence: 4, 11, 22, 37, 56

Find an expression, in terms of n, for the nth term of this sequence.
answer: 2n2 + n + 1 — the differences are 7, 11, 15, 19 and the second difference is 4, so the n2 coefficient is half of that, 2. Taking 2n2 = 2, 8, 18, 32, 50 away leaves 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, which is n + 1. It reproduces all five terms
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
L is the circle with equation x2 + y2 = 4 and P(3⁄2, √7⁄2) is a point on L.

Find an equation of the tangent to L at the point P.
answer: 3x + √7y = 8, that is y = (8 − 3x)⁄√7 — the tangent is perpendicular to the radius OP, whose gradient is (√7⁄2) ÷ (3⁄2) = √7⁄3. The negative reciprocal is −3⁄√7, and putting P into y = mx + c finishes it. Two checks: P really is on the circle, since 9⁄4 + 7⁄4 = 4, and P satisfies the tangent, since 4.5 + 3.5 = 8
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
ℰ = {odd numbers less than 30}
A = {3, 9, 15, 21, 27}
B = {5, 15, 25}

Complete the Venn diagram to represent this information.
answer: 15 goes in the overlap, because it is the only number in both lists. 3, 9, 21 and 27 go in A alone and 5, 25 in B alone. The eight odd numbers under 30 that are in neither — 1, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29 — go in the rectangle outside both circles, and leaving those out is what loses the last mark
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
A number is chosen at random from the universal set, ℰ.

What is the probability that the number is in the set A ∪ B?
answer: <sup>7</sup>⁄<sub>15</sub> — ∪ is union, so count every number in either circle: 3, 5, 9, 15, 21, 25, 27 is 7 of them. The odd numbers below 30 run 1, 3, 5, …, 29, which is 15 numbers, not 30
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Solve the simultaneous equations

3x + y = −4
3x − 4y = 6
answer: x = −2⁄3, y = −2 — the x terms already match, so subtracting the second equation from the first gives 5y = −10. Putting y = −2 back into 3x + y = −4 gives 3x = −2. A fractional answer here is right, not a mistake
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The table shows some information about the dress sizes of 25 women: size 8 — 2 women, size 10 — 9 women, size 12 — 8 women, size 14 — 6 women.

Find the median dress size.
answer: 12 — with 25 values the median is the 13th. Running totals are 2, 11, 19, 25, so the 11th woman is the last size 10 and the 13th falls in the size 12 group
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
3 of the 25 women have a shoe size of 7. Zoe says that if you choose at random one of the 25 women, the probability that she has either a shoe size of 7 or a dress size of 14 is 9⁄25 because 3⁄25 + 6⁄25 = 9⁄25.

Is Zoe correct? You must give a reason for your answer.
answer: No. Adding probabilities only works for events that cannot both happen, and these can: a woman could take a size 14 dress AND a size 7 shoe, and Zoe has counted her twice. Nothing in the question says the two groups are separate
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Daniel bakes 420 cakes. He bakes only vanilla cakes, banana cakes, lemon cakes and chocolate cakes. 2⁄7 of the cakes are vanilla cakes. 35% of the cakes are banana cakes. The ratio of the number of lemon cakes to the number of chocolate cakes is 4 : 5

Work out the number of lemon cakes Daniel bakes.
answer: 68 — vanilla is <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>7</sub> of 420 = 120 and banana is 35% of 420 = 147, so lemon and chocolate share 420 − 120 − 147 = 153. Split in 4 : 5 that is 9 parts of 17, and lemon takes 4 of them: 153 ÷ 9 × 4
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
In the diagram, AB, BC and CD are three sides of a regular polygon P. At the point B a square, polygon P and a regular 12-sided polygon meet, and the same three shapes meet at C.

Show that polygon P is a hexagon. You must show your working.
answer: The three interior angles at B make a full turn, 360°. The square gives 90° and the regular 12-gon gives (12 − 2) × 180 ÷ 12 = 150°, so polygon P’s interior angle is 360 − 90 − 150 = 120°. Its exterior angle is therefore 60°, and 360 ÷ 60 = 6 sides — a hexagon
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The density of apple juice is 1.05 grams per cm3. The density of fruit syrup is 1.4 grams per cm3. The density of carbonated water is 0.99 grams per cm3. 25 cm3 of apple juice are mixed with 15 cm3 of fruit syrup and 280 cm3 of carbonated water to make a drink with a volume of 320 cm3.

Work out the density of the drink. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
answer: 1.01 g/cm<sup>3</sup> — densities cannot be averaged, but masses can be added. 25 × 1.05 = 26.25 g, 15 × 1.4 = 21 g and 280 × 0.99 = 277.2 g, giving 324.45 g in 320 cm<sup>3</sup>. 324.45 ÷ 320 = 1.01390…
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
ABC is a right-angled triangle, with the right angle at B. CA = 15 cm and the angle at C is 23°.

Calculate the length of AB. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
answer: 5.86 cm — the right angle is at B, so CA is the hypotenuse. AB is opposite the 23° angle, so sin is the ratio to use: AB = 15 sin 23° = 5.8609…
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
A square, with sides of length x cm, is inside a circle. Each vertex of the square is on the circumference of the circle. The area of the circle is 49 cm2.

Work out the value of x. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
answer: 5.58 — 49 is the area in cm2, not 49π, so πr2 = 49 gives r = √(49 ÷ π) = 3.9493… and the diameter is 7.8986… cm. The square’s diagonal IS that diameter, so by Pythagoras x2 + x2 = 7.8986…2 and x = 7.8986… ÷ √2 = 5.5851…
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The box plot shows information about the distribution of the amounts of money spent by some male students on their holidays. Read from the scale, the five values are: smallest £20, lower quartile £150, median £250, upper quartile £330, largest £750.

Work out the interquartile range for the amounts of money spent by these male students.
answer: £180 — the interquartile range is the width of the BOX, upper quartile minus lower quartile: 330 − 150. It is not the whole range, and the whiskers play no part in it
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The table shows information about the distribution of the amounts of money spent by some female students on their holidays: smallest £60, lower quartile £180, median £300, upper quartile £350, largest £650.

On the grid above, draw a box plot for the information in the table.
answer: A box from 180 to 350 with the median line at 300, and whiskers out to 60 on the left and 650 on the right, drawn below the male plot on the same scale. The five values go straight on: nothing needs calculating here
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Chris says, “The box plots show that the female students spent more money than the male students.”

Is Chris correct? Give a reason for your answer.
answer: Either answer earns the mark if the reason comes from the plots. For Chris: the female median is £300 against the male £250, so on average the female students did spend more. Against Chris: the male plot reaches £750 where the female one stops at £650, so the biggest spenders were male. What is not allowed is an opinion with no figure from the plots behind it
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Naoby invests £6000 for 5 years. The investment gets compound interest of x% per annum. At the end of 5 years the investment is worth £8029.35

Work out the value of x.
answer: 6 — five years of compound interest multiply by the same factor five times, so 6000 × k5 = 8029.35 and k5 = 1.338225. Taking the fifth root gives k = 1.06, which is a 6% rise each year. Checking forwards: 6000 × 1.065 = 8029.35
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Jeff is choosing a shrub and a rose tree for his garden. At the garden centre there are 17 different types of shrubs and some rose trees. Jeff says, “There are 215 different ways to choose one shrub and one rose tree.”

Could Jeff be correct? You must show how you get your answer.
answer: No. One of each means the numbers multiply, so the total must be 17 × (number of rose trees) — a multiple of 17. 215 ÷ 17 = 12.6…, which is not a whole number, so no number of rose trees gives 215. (17 × 12 = 204 and 17 × 13 = 221 straddle it.)
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The points A, B, C and D lie in order on a straight line. AB : BD = 1 : 5 and AC : CD = 7 : 11

Work out AB : BC : CD
answer: 3 : 4 : 11 — both ratios split the same whole AD, into 6 parts and into 18 parts, so scale the first up to eighteenths: AB : BD = 3 : 15. Now AB = 3 and AC = 7 measured from A, so BC = 7 − 3 = 4, and CD = 11. Check: 3 + 4 + 11 = 18
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The grid shows a shaded triangular region bounded by three lines: a line through (0, 1) and (2, 2), a line through the origin at 45°, and a horizontal line through (0, −2).

Write down the three inequalities that define the shaded region.
answer: y ≥ −2, y ≤ ½x + 1 and y ≥ x. Find each line first: the shallow one cuts the y-axis at 1 and rises 1 for every 2 across, so y = ½x + 1; the steep one passes through the origin and (2, 2), so y = x; the flat one is y = −2. Then test one point inside, say (−3, −1): it is below the first line, above the second and above −2. All three lines are solid, so all three are ≤ or ≥ rather than strict
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html: Simplify (x2 − 16) ⁄ (2x2 − 5x − 12)
answer: (x + 4) ⁄ (2x + 3) — the top is a difference of two squares, (x − 4)(x + 4). The bottom factorises as (2x + 3)(x − 4), since 2 × −12 = −24 splits as +3 and −8. The (x − 4) cancels
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html: Make v the subject of the formula w = 15(t − 2v) ⁄ v
answer: v = 15t ⁄ (w + 30) — v appears twice, so gather it. Multiply through by v: wv = 15t − 30v. Move every v term to one side: wv + 30v = 15t, then factorise, v(w + 30) = 15t
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
In triangle ABC, BC = (x + 3) metres, AB = (2x − 1) metres and the angle ABC between them is 45°. The area of triangle ABC is 6√2 m2.

Calculate the value of x. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
answer: 2.63 — the two given sides enclose the given angle, so area = ½ab sin C: ½(x + 3)(2x − 1) sin 45° = 6√2. Since sin 45° = √2⁄2, the √2 cancels off both sides and leaves (x + 3)(2x − 1) = 24, so 2x2 + 5x − 27 = 0. The formula gives x = (−5 + √241) ⁄ 4 = 2.6310…; the other root, −5.13, would make a negative length
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Using xn+1 = −2 − 4 ⁄ xn2 with x0 = −2.5

Find the values of x1, x2 and x3
answer: x1 = −2.64, x2 = −2.5739…, x3 = −2.6037… — feed each answer straight back in. −2 − 4 ÷ (−2.5)2 = −2 − 0.64 = −2.64; then −2 − 4 ÷ 2.642; then again. Squaring kills the minus sign, so the fraction is always subtracted
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html: Explain the relationship between the values of x1, x2 and x3 and the equation x3 + 2x2 + 4 = 0
answer: They are converging on a solution of that equation. The iteration IS the equation rearranged: x3 + 2x2 + 4 = 0 gives x2(x + 2) = −4, so x + 2 = −4 ⁄ x2 and x = −2 − 4 ⁄ x2. The values oscillate either side of the root and close in on about −2.59
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
A train travelled along a track in 110 minutes, correct to the nearest 5 minutes. Jake finds out that the track is 270 km long. He assumes that the track has been measured correct to the nearest 10 km.

Could the average speed of the train have been greater than 160 km/h? You must show how you get your answer.
answer: No. Speed is greatest when the distance is at its largest and the time at its smallest, so take 275 km (the upper bound of 270 to the nearest 10) and 107.5 minutes (the lower bound of 110 to the nearest 5). 107.5 minutes is 107.5 ÷ 60 = 1.79166… hours, and 275 ÷ 1.79166… = 153.48… km/h. Even the fastest the figures allow is under 160
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Jake’s assumption was wrong. The track was measured correct to the nearest 5 km.

Explain how this could affect your decision in part (a).
answer: It does not change the decision. The nearest 5 km puts the upper bound at 272.5 km instead of 275, which is a SMALLER distance, so the fastest possible speed drops to 272.5 ÷ 1.79166… = 152.09… km/h — still under 160. A tighter measurement can only narrow the bounds, never widen them
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
A, B and C are points on a circle of radius 5 cm, centre O. DA and DC are tangents to the circle and DO = 9 cm. B lies on the far side of the circle from D.

Work out the length of arc ABC. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
answer: 21.6 cm — a tangent meets the radius at 90°, so OAD is right-angled with hypotenuse OD = 9 and OA = 5. cos(angle AOD) = 5 ÷ 9 gives 56.25°, and by symmetry angle AOC = 112.5°. Arc ABC goes the long way round through B, so its angle is 360 − 112.5 = 247.49°, and the arc is 247.49… ÷ 360 × 2π × 5 = 21.598…. Taking the minor arc instead gives 9.82, and that is the trap
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html: Solve 2x2 + 3x − 2 > 0
answer: x < −2 or x > ½ — factorise to (2x − 1)(x + 2) > 0, with roots ½ and −2. The curve opens upwards, so it is ABOVE the axis outside the roots, not between them. The answer is two separate pieces, and writing it as a single chain like −2 < x < ½ is the region where it is negative
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The equation of a curve is y = ax. A is the point where the curve intersects the y-axis.

State the coordinates of A.
answer: (0, 1) — the y-axis is x = 0, and a0 = 1 for every value of a. That is why every exponential curve of this form passes through the same point
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017

html:
The equation of circle C is x2 + y2 = 16. The circle C is translated by the vector (3, 0) to give circle B.

Draw a sketch of circle B. Label with coordinates the centre of circle B and any points of intersection with the x-axis.
answer: A circle of radius 4 centred at (3, 0), crossing the x-axis at (−1, 0) and (7, 0). C is centred on the origin with radius √16 = 4, and the vector moves it 3 to the right and none up. The crossings are then 3 − 4 and 3 + 4
name: Paper 3 (Calculator) — June 2017
subject: Maths

html: Write 36 as a product of its prime factors.
answer: 2<sup>2</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup>, that is 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 — keep halving and then dividing by 3: 36 = 2 × 18 = 2 × 2 × 9 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. A product means it must be written as a multiplication, not as a list
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Kiaria is 7 years older than Jay. Martha is twice as old as Kiaria. The sum of their three ages is 77

Find the ratio of Jay’s age to Kiaria’s age to Martha’s age.
answer: 14 : 21 : 42, or 2 : 3 : 6 — the mark scheme prints the first and accepts any equivalent, so a simplified answer is right too. Call Jay’s age j. Kiaria is j + 7 and Martha is 2(j + 7) = 2j + 14, so 4j + 21 = 77 and j = 14. The ages are 14, 21 and 42, and every one divides by 7
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
ABCD is a parallelogram. EDC is a straight line. F is the point on AD so that BFE is a straight line. Angle EFD = 35° and angle DCB = 75°.

Show that angle ABF = 70°. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
answer: Angle AFB = 35°, vertically opposite angle EFD (AD and BE are both straight lines crossing at F). Angle BAF = angle BAD = 75°, because opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so it matches angle DCB. Then angle ABF = 180 − 35 − 75 = 70°, because angles in a triangle add to 180°. The marks are for the REASONS as much as the numbers

html: Work out an estimate for the mean of the weekly earnings.
answer: £365 — grouped data has no individual values, so use the midpoint of each class: 200, 300, 400, 500, 600. Then 200 × 1 + 300 × 11 + 400 × 5 + 500 × 0 + 600 × 3 = 7300, and 7300 ÷ 20. The empty class still counts as a class but adds nothing

html:
Nadiya says, “The mean may not be the best average to use to represent this information.”

Do you agree with Nadiya? You must justify your answer.
answer: Yes. The three people earning over £550 drag the mean up: £365 is above the class that 11 of the 20 people are in. The median or the modal class, both in 250 < x ≤ 350, describe the group better. A bare “yes” with no figure earns nothing

html:
A rectangle has one pair of opposite sides labelled (2x + 6) and (5x − 9), and the other side labelled y. All measurements are in centimetres. The area of the rectangle is 48 cm2.

Show that y = 3
answer: The two labelled sides are OPPOSITE sides of a rectangle, so they are equal: 2x + 6 = 5x − 9 gives 3x = 15 and x = 5. Both sides are then 16 cm. Area = 16y = 48, so y = 3. Spotting that the two expressions are equal is the whole question

html: Write these numbers in order of size, starting with the smallest number: 0.24̇6̇, 0.246̇, 0.2̇46̇, 0.246 — that is, 0.2464646…, 0.2466666…, 0.246246246… and 0.246 exactly.
answer: 0.246, then 0.2̇46̇, then 0.24̇6̇, then 0.246̇. Write each one out to enough places and compare digit by digit: 0.246000, 0.246246, 0.246464, 0.246666. They agree to three decimal places, so the fourth digit decides it — 0, 2, 4, 6

html:
James and Peter cycled along the same 50 km route. James took 2½ hours to cycle the 50 km. Peter started to cycle 5 minutes after James started to cycle. Peter caught up with James when they had both cycled 15 km. James and Peter both cycled at constant speeds.

Work out Peter’s speed.
answer: 22.5 km/h — James rode 50 km in 2.5 hours, so 20 km/h, and 15 km took him 15 ÷ 20 = 0.75 hours = 45 minutes. Peter started 5 minutes later and arrived at the same moment, so he covered the same 15 km in 40 minutes = <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> hour. 15 ÷ <sup>2</sup>⁄<sub>3</sub> = 22.5
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html: Write down the value of 100½
answer: 10 — a power of ½ is a square root, and √100 = 10
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html: Find the value of 1252⁄3
answer: 25 — the bottom of the fraction is the root and the top is the power, so take the cube root first and square it: ∛125 = 5, then 5<sup>2</sup> = 25. Doing it the other way round works too but means cube-rooting 15 625
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
3 teas and 2 coffees have a total cost of £7.80. 5 teas and 4 coffees have a total cost of £14.20

Work out the cost of one tea and the cost of one coffee.
answer: Tea £1.40, coffee £1.80 — with t and c, 3t + 2c = 7.80 and 5t + 4c = 14.20. Doubling the first gives 6t + 4c = 15.60, and subtracting the second leaves t = 1.40. Then 4.20 + 2c = 7.80. Check both: 3(1.40) + 2(1.80) = 7.80 and 5(1.40) + 4(1.80) = 14.20
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html: Draw a box plot for this information.
answer: A box from 161 to 168 with the median at 165, and whiskers to 154 and 174. Two of the five values have to be worked out first: the upper quartile is the lower quartile plus the interquartile range, 161 + 7 = 168, and the greatest height is the least plus the range, 154 + 20 = 174
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
A second box plot shows the heights, in cm, of a group of Year 7 girls. Read from the grid, its five values are: least 146, lower quartile 154.5, median 157.5, upper quartile 165, greatest 170.5.

Compare the distribution of heights of the Year 7 girls with the distribution of heights of the Year 11 girls.
answer: Two comparisons are wanted, one about average and one about spread, and at least one of them has to be in context. The Year 11 median (165 cm) is higher than the Year 7 median (157.5 cm), so the Year 11 girls are taller on average. The Year 11 interquartile range (7 cm) is smaller than the Year 7 one (165 − 154.5 = 10.5 cm), so the Year 11 heights are less spread out. Ranges do the second job too: 20 cm against 170.5 − 146 = 24.5 cm
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
A factory makes 450 pies every day. The pies are chicken pies or steak pies. Each day Milo takes a sample of 15 pies to check. The proportion of the pies in his sample that are chicken is the same as the proportion of the pies made that day that are chicken. On Monday Milo calculated that he needed exactly 4 chicken pies in his sample.

Work out the total number of chicken pies that were made on Monday.
answer: 120 — the sample is <sup>4</sup>⁄<sub>15</sub> chicken, so the day’s pies are too: <sup>4</sup>⁄<sub>15</sub> × 450. Or scale up: 15 goes into 450 thirty times, so 4 × 30
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
On Tuesday, the number of steak pies Milo needs in his sample is 6 correct to the nearest whole number. Milo takes at random a pie from the 450 pies made on Tuesday.

Work out the lower bound of the probability that the pie is a steak pie.
answer: <sup>11</sup>⁄<sub>30</sub>, about 0.367 — “6 to the nearest whole number” means anything from 5.5 up to 6.5, so the smallest the sample count could be is 5.5. The probability is that share of the sample, 5.5 ÷ 15 = <sup>11</sup>⁄<sub>30</sub>. The 450 never enters it — the proportion is the same in the sample and in the day’s pies
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
The ratio (y + x) : (y − x) is equivalent to k : 1

Show that y = x(k + 1) ⁄ (k − 1)
answer: A ratio equal to k : 1 means the first part divided by the second is k, so (y + x) ⁄ (y − x) = k and y + x = k(y − x) = ky − kx. Collect the y terms on one side and the x terms on the other: x + kx = ky − y, so x(k + 1) = y(k − 1)
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
x = 0.43̇6̇, that is 0.4363636… with the 36 repeating.

Prove algebraically that x can be written as 24⁄55
answer: Multiply by two powers of ten whose decimal parts match, then subtract. 10x = 4.363636… and 1000x = 436.363636…, so 990x = 432 exactly. Then x = 432⁄990, and dividing top and bottom by 18 gives 24⁄55. Picking 10x and 1000x rather than x and 100x is what lines the recurring parts up, because the 4 does not repeat
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
y is directly proportional to ∛x. y = 11⁄6 when x = 8

Find the value of y when x = 64
answer: 21⁄3, that is 7⁄3 — the variable is the CUBE ROOT of x, not x cubed. So y = k∛x, and 7⁄6 = k × 2 gives k = 7⁄12. At x = 64 the cube root is 4, so y = 7⁄12 × 4. Or note that x going 8 → 64 doubles the cube root, so it doubles y
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html: n is an integer. Prove algebraically that the sum of ½n(n + 1) and ½(n + 1)(n + 2) is always a square number.
answer: Both terms share ½(n + 1), so factorise rather than expand: ½(n + 1)[n + (n + 2)] = ½(n + 1)(2n + 2) = ½(n + 1) × 2(n + 1) = (n + 1)2. Since n is an integer so is n + 1, and a square of an integer is a square number
name: Paper 1 (Non-Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Shape P is the triangle with vertices (2, 7), (2, 3) and (4, 3).

Enlarge shape P by scale factor −½ with centre of enlargement (0, 0). Label your image Q.
answer: The triangle with vertices (−1, −3½), (−1, −1½) and (−2, −1½). With the centre at the origin, just multiply every coordinate by −½. The minus sign puts the image on the opposite side of the centre, turned through 180°, and the ½ halves every length

html:
ABCD is a rectangle. A, E and B are points on the straight line L with equation x + 2y = 12, where E is on the y-axis and B is on the x-axis. A and D are points on the straight line M. AE = EB.

Find an equation for M.
answer: y = 2x + 36. L cuts the axes at E(0, 6) and B(12, 0), and AE = EB makes E the midpoint of AB, so A = 2E − B = (−12, 12). AD is a side of a rectangle meeting AB, so M is perpendicular to L: L has gradient −½, so M has gradient 2. Then 12 = 2(−12) + c. The diagram is not to scale, which is why A looks nearer the origin than it is

The table shows some values of x and y that satisfy the equation y = a cos x° + b.

x0306090120150180
y31 + √32101 − √3−1

Find the value of y when x = 45
answer: 1 + √2 — find a and b from the two easy columns. cos 90° = 0, so the x = 90 entry gives b = 1 straight away; cos 0° = 1, so a + b = 3 and a = 2. Then y = 2 cos 45° + 1, and cos 45° = √2⁄2, so the 2 cancels. Check against x = 60: 2 × ½ + 1 = 2, as the table says

html: Show that (6 − √8) ⁄ (√2 − 1) can be written in the form a + b√2 where a and b are integers.
answer: 2 + 4√2. Simplify √8 = 2√2 first, then rationalise by multiplying top and bottom by √2 + 1. The bottom becomes (√2)<sup>2</sup> − 1 = 1, which is why the answer comes out with integers. The top is (6 − 2√2)(√2 + 1) = 6√2 + 6 − 4 − 2√2 = 2 + 4√2. Check on a calculator: both sides are 7.657

html:
The two triangles in the diagram are similar. B lies on AC and E lies on AD, with AB = 8 cm, BC = x cm, AE = 12 cm and ED = 3 cm.

There are two possible values of x. Work out each of these values. State any assumptions you make in your working.
answer: x = 2 or x = 14.5. Both triangles share the angle at A, and AC = 8 + x while AD = 15. Which pairs of sides correspond depends on an assumption. Assuming BE is parallel to CD, so angle ABE = angle ACD: 8 ⁄ (8 + x) = 12 ⁄ 15, giving x = 2. Assuming instead that angle ABE = angle ADC: 8 ⁄ 15 = 12 ⁄ (8 + x), giving 8 + x = 22.5 and x = 14.5. The mark for the assumption is a real mark, not a formality

A rectangle measures (3x − 2) by (x − 1), and a right-angled triangle has perpendicular sides 2x and x. All measurements are in centimetres. The area of the rectangle is greater than the area of the triangle.

Find the set of possible values of x.
answer: x > 2. The rectangle is (3x − 2)(x − 1) = 3x2 − 5x + 2 and the triangle is ½ × x × 2x = x2, so 2x2 − 5x + 2 > 0, which factorises to (2x − 1)(x − 2) > 0 with roots ½ and 2. That inequality alone allows x < ½ as well — but the rectangle’s side is x − 1, which must be positive, so x > 1 and that branch is impossible. Throwing it away is the last mark

html: Solve 5x − 6 = 3(x − 1)
answer: x = 1.5, or 3⁄2 — expand the bracket first: 5x − 6 = 3x − 3. Then 2x = 3. Check by substituting: both sides come to 1.5

html:
Emily buys a pack of 12 bottles of water. The pack costs £5.64. Emily sells all 12 bottles for 50p each.

Work out Emily’s percentage profit. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
answer: 6.4% — she takes 12 × 50p = £6.00, so the profit is £6.00 − £5.64 = £0.36. Percentage profit is measured against what she PAID: 0.36 ÷ 5.64 × 100 = 6.382…. Dividing by 6.00 instead gives 6.0%, and that is the common slip
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Hasmeet walks once round a circle with diameter 80 metres. There are 8 points equally spaced on the circumference of the circle.

Find the distance Hasmeet walks between one point and the next point.
answer: 31.4 m — the whole way round is πd = π × 80 = 251.3… m, and eight equal gaps means dividing by 8. Using the radius by mistake halves it
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Four of the points are moved, so they are no longer equally spaced. Hasmeet walks once round the circle again.

Has the mean distance that Hasmeet walks between one point and the next point changed? You must give a reason for your answer.
answer: No. The mean is the total distance divided by the number of gaps, and moving the points changes neither: it is still the same circumference shared between the same 8 gaps. The individual distances change, but their mean cannot
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
There are only blue cubes, yellow cubes and green cubes in a bag. There are twice as many blue cubes as yellow cubes, and four times as many green cubes as blue cubes. Hannah takes at random a cube from the bag.

Work out the probability that Hannah takes a yellow cube.
answer: <sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>11</sub> — build the ratio from the smallest group. Call yellow 1 part; blue is twice that, 2 parts; green is four times BLUE, so 8 parts, not 4. That is 1 : 2 : 8, eleven parts in all. Reading “four times as many green as blue” as four times yellow is the trap
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Trapezium T has vertices (2, −1), (4, −1), (5, −2) and (2, −2).

Rotate trapezium T 180° about the origin. Label the new trapezium A.
answer: The trapezium with vertices (−2, 1), (−4, 1), (−5, 2) and (−2, 2). A half turn about the origin sends every point (x, y) to (−x, −y), so no direction needs deciding — clockwise and anticlockwise agree
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html: Translate trapezium T by the vector (−1, −3). Label the new trapezium B.
answer: The trapezium with vertices (1, −4), (3, −4), (4, −5) and (1, −5). The top number of the vector moves it left or right and the bottom number up or down, so this is 1 left and 3 down
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
p3 × px = p9

Find the value of x.
answer: 6 — multiplying powers of the same letter adds the indices, so 3 + x = 9
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
(72)y = 710

Find the value of y.
answer: 5 — a power raised to a power multiplies the indices, so 2y = 10
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
100a × 1000b can be written in the form 10w.

Show that w = 2a + 3b
answer: Write both bases as powers of 10 first: 100 = 102 and 1000 = 103. Then 100a = (102)a = 102a and 1000b = 103b. Multiplying adds the indices, giving 102a + 3b
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
ABCD is a trapezium with BC parallel to AD. AD = 24 cm, BC = 10 cm, AB = 7.5 cm and the perpendicular height from BC down to AD is 6 cm.

Work out the size of angle CDA. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
answer: 32.3° — drop a perpendicular from B: by Pythagoras its foot is √(7.52 − 62) = √20.25 = 4.5 cm from A. C is then 4.5 + 10 = 14.5 cm along from A, so the perpendicular from C lands 24 − 14.5 = 9.5 cm from D. In that right-angled triangle tan D = 6 ÷ 9.5, so D = 32.275…°
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html:
Use your calculator to work out √((sin 25° + sin 40°) ⁄ (cos 25° − cos 40°))

Write down all the figures on your calculator display.
answer: 2.756039570… — the answer to as many figures as the display shows. Put the whole fraction under the root in one go rather than rounding the top and bottom first; rounding part way is what loses the marks on this kind of question
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
subject: Maths

html: Write your answer to part (a) correct to 2 decimal places.
answer: 2.76 — the third decimal is 6, so the second rounds up

html:
Yesterday it took 5 cleaners 4½ hours to clean all the rooms in a hotel. There are only 3 cleaners to clean all the rooms in the hotel today. Each cleaner is paid £8.20 for each hour or part of an hour they work.

How much will each cleaner be paid today?
answer: £65.60 — the job is 5 × 4.5 = 22.5 cleaner-hours however many people do it, so 3 cleaners take 22.5 ÷ 3 = 7.5 hours each. “Each hour or PART of an hour” rounds that up to 8 hours, so 8 × 8.20. Paying for 7.5 hours gives £61.50 and misses the point of that sentence
name: Paper 2 (Calculator) — November 2017
