How does the writer use language here to describe the effects of the heat?

You could include the writer’s choice of:

  • words and phrases
  • language features and techniques
  • sentence forms.

subject: English Language
name: Paper 1: Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing — May 2024
html:
You now need to think about the whole of the source.

This text is taken from the middle of a novel.

How has the writer structured the text to interest you as a reader?

You could write about:

  • what the writer focuses your attention on at the beginning of the source
  • how and why the writer changes this focus as the source develops
  • any other structural features that interest you.

subject: English Language
name: Paper 1: Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing — May 2024
html:
Focus this part of your answer on the second part of the source, from line 18 to the end.

A student said, “Dick’s anger towards Mary is really unfair. The writer makes it clear that Mary is totally powerless in this relationship.”

To what extent do you agree?

In your response you could:

  • consider whether Dick’s anger is unfair
  • evaluate how the writer presents Mary and Dick’s relationship
  • support your response with references to the text.

subject: English Language
name: Paper 1: Explorations in Creative Reading and Writing — May 2024
html:
A magazine has asked for contributions for their creative writing section.

Either

Write a description of a very hot place as suggested by this picture:

or

Write a story about a disagreement.

(24 marks for content and organisation, 16 marks for technical accuracy)

The picture above is drawn here. AQA prints a photograph of the same scene and it is third-party copyright, so what is on this card is an impression of it — the hot sky, the sun, the hazy ranges and the bare ground — rather than the photograph itself.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Wind turbines may generate electricity when the electricity is not needed. Two methods that can be used to store the energy from the turbine are:

Method A: Heating water to a high temperature.
Method B: Pumping water uphill into a reservoir.

Which energy store increases when water is heated?
answer: Thermal (internal) energy store — or the kinetic store of the water particles

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Which energy store increases when water is pumped uphill into a reservoir?
answer: Gravitational potential energy store

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 1 shows information about the two methods of storing energy.

MethodEnergy stored per 100 kg of water in kJPercentage of stored energy wastedInstallation
A: Increasing water temperature by 80 °C33 60040%Anywhere
B: Pumping water uphill to a height of 500 m49025%High mountains

Compare the advantages and disadvantages of the two methods of storing energy. Include calculations in your answer.
answer: Level-marked out of 4. Method A: useful energy per 100 kg = 20 160 kJ, wasted = 13 440 kJ, efficiency 60%; stores far more energy per 100 kg, but the hot water needs insulating. Method B: useful = 367.5 kJ, wasted = 122.5 kJ, efficiency 75%; more efficient, but needs a high mountain site. A Level 2 answer uses the table in a calculation that compares the two.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Decreasing the amount of carbon dioxide released by different activities will help slow down climate change. Transport and generating electricity are the two activities that released the largest amounts of carbon dioxide in the UK in 2018.

Explain one change that would reduce the amount of carbon dioxide released by each activity.
answer: Transport: stop burning petrol or diesel, and use electric or hydrogen cars, a bicycle, public transport or walking instead. Generating electricity: stop using coal, oil or gas, and use renewables or nuclear instead — or use fewer appliances, to cut the demand for electricity generated from fossil fuels. Two marks for each activity.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The process of nuclear fission is used in nuclear power stations. Figure 2 shows the process of nuclear fission.

Complete the sentences. Choose answers from the box.

electrons   gamma rays   neutrons   nuclei   protons

In nuclear power stations, energy is released from uranium ............... .
The uranium in Figure 2 splits into two parts and releases three ............... .
The process of nuclear fission releases electromagnetic radiation in the form of ............... .
answer: nuclei; neutrons; gamma (rays) — this order only
examiner_note: Figure 2, the fission diagram, is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Write down the equation which links energy (E), power (P) and time (t).
answer: energy = power × time, or E = P × t

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: A nuclear power station has a power output of 500 MW. Calculate the energy output in 3600 s. Give your answer in J.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Radioactive waste produced by nuclear power stations has a long half-life. Suggest one precaution taken to reduce the hazard caused by radioactive waste from power stations.
answer: Any one of: bury it; put it in cooling ponds; transport it in secure vessels; store it in metal containers; cover it in concrete

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Nuclear power stations do not generate electricity every day of the year. One nuclear power station generated electricity for 92% of a year.

one year = 365 days

Calculate the number of days during the year that the nuclear power station generated electricity.
answer: 335.8 days (335 or 336 also accepted)

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated how the length of a wire affects the resistance of the wire at constant temperature. Figure 3 shows the circuit used.

The student plotted a graph of resistance against the length of wire. Describe a method the student could have used to collect the data needed to plot the graph.
answer: Level-marked out of 6. Measure the length of wire between the crocodile clips with a ruler; vary the length by moving the clips; measure the current with an ammeter and the potential difference with a voltmeter; record both for each length; use V = IR to calculate the resistance for each length. Also: repeat and mean the readings, remove anomalies, keep the current low so the wire does not heat, and disconnect the circuit between readings.
examiner_note: Figure 3, the circuit diagram, is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which graph shows the relationship between the resistance of a wire at constant temperature and its length?

Tick one box.
answer: The straight line through the origin — resistance is directly proportional to length
examiner_note: The four graphs to choose between are artwork in the PDF. The mark scheme prints the answer as a straight line from the origin, resistance against length, which was read off a render of the scheme rather than described from memory.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The student used a cell that had a potential difference of 1.50 V. Explain why the cell was not an electrical hazard to the student in the investigation.
answer: The potential difference is very low, so there is no risk of electric shock

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A static electricity generator has a rubber belt turned by a motor, and as the belt moves charge is transferred from the belt to the metal dome. Figure 5 shows a student touching the metal dome. The dome is negatively charged.

Explain why the student’s hair stands up on end.
answer: Electrons are transferred to the student, so her hair is negatively charged, and like charges repel
examiner_note: Figures 4 and 5 are photographs in the PDF and are not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The charged metal dome creates an electric field. What is an electric field?
answer: The region around a charged object where another charged object experiences a force

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: How does the electric field strength vary as the distance from the charged metal dome increases?
answer: It decreases

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 6 shows the negatively charged metal dome and an earthed conductor. When the earthed conductor is moved towards the metal dome, there is a spark between the dome and the earthed conductor.

The spark transfers 0.60 J of energy, and 2.0 µC of charge is transferred from the dome to the earthed conductor. Calculate the potential difference between the metal dome and the earthed conductor.
examiner_note: Figure 6 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which of the following changes would increase the distance a spark can jump between the dome and the earthed conductor? Tick one box.

  • Decreased charge on the metal dome
  • Decreased electric field strength
  • Decreased electrical resistance of air
  • Decreased potential difference
answer: Decreased electrical resistance of air

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: A vending machine is connected to the mains electricity supply. What is the frequency and the potential difference of the mains electricity supply in the UK?
answer: Frequency = 50 Hz; potential difference = 230 V

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The vending machine identifies the value of a coin by measuring the resistance of the coin. The power dissipated by the coin is 340 mW when the current in the coin is 0.75 A. Calculate the resistance of the coin.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Coins that are dirty are not recognised by the vending machine. Suggest one reason why.
answer: The dirt changes the measured resistance of the coin, so it does not match the resistance expected for that coin

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 8 shows part of a different circuit that is used to monitor the temperature inside the vending machine. The circuit symbol for a thermistor has not been included.

Draw the circuit symbol for a thermistor in the box below.
answer: The resistor rectangle with a diagonal line drawn across it, turning horizontal at the lower left
examiner_note: Figure 8 is a circuit diagram in the PDF and is not transcribed. The symbol was read off a render of the mark scheme.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 shows how the resistance of the thermistor varies with temperature. The cooling system inside the vending machine turns on when the temperature of the thermistor is above 20 °C.

Determine the potential difference across the thermistor when the temperature is 20 °C.
answer: 2.0 V (1.8 V to 2.2 V accepted)
examiner_note: Figure 9 is a graph in the PDF and is not transcribed, and Figure 8 carries the rest of the circuit. The mark scheme's own working gives the values the two figures supply: the thermistor reads about 80 ohms at 20 degrees Celsius, the fixed resistor is 400 ohms, and the supply is 12 V.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
In a ride at a theme park, a person is strapped into a pod that is attached to two stretched bungee cords. The bungee cords behave like springs.

Which energy store increases as the bungee cords are stretched?
answer: Elastic potential energy store
examiner_note: Figure 10 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
When the pod is released, the pod accelerates upwards. Before the pod is released the extension of each of the two bungee cords is 8.0 m. The spring constant of each bungee cord is 735 N/m. The mass of the pod is 240 kg.

gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg

Calculate the maximum height reached by the pod.
answer: 20 m. One cord stores 0.5 × 735 × 8.0² = 23 520 J, so the two store 47 040 J; 47 040 = 240 × 9.8 × h

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The actual maximum height reached by the pod will be lower than the correct answer to Question 06.2 Explain why.
answer: Air resistance opposes the pod's motion upwards, so not all of the elastic potential energy is transferred to the gravitational potential store

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student used a measuring cylinder containing some water to measure the volume of a metal ring. When measuring the volume, the student’s eye was in line with the level of the water.

Which type of error would have been caused if the student’s eye was not in line with the level of the water? Tick one box.

  • Random error
  • Systematic error
  • Zero error
answer: Random error
examiner_note: Figure 11 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The student tied a piece of thick string to the metal ring and lowered the ring into the water. Suggest one reason why the student should have used thin string instead of thick string.
answer: Thin string would affect the volume measurement less — it displaces less water

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 2 shows the results.

Volume of water in cm³Volume of water and ring in cm³Volume of ring in cm³
5.05.40.4

The true volume of the ring was 0.44 cm³. Even without using the string, the measuring cylinder could not give an accurate value for the volume of the ring. Give one reason why.
answer: The measuring cylinder cannot be read to two decimal places — its resolution is 0.2 cm³

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The student used a balance to measure the mass of the ring. After the ring was removed from the balance, the reading on the balance was 0.02 g. How could the student use the readings from the balance to determine the correct mass of the ring?
answer: Subtract 0.02 g from the measured value

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The student determined that the density of the ring was 21 500 kg/m³. The volume of the ring was 0.44 cm³. Calculate the mass of the ring. Give your answer in kg.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated how the pressure in a fixed mass of air varies with the volume of the air. When the plunger was pushed slowly into the syringe, the pressure in the syringe increased. The temperature of the air remained constant.

Explain why the pressure increased.
answer: The air particles are closer together, so the frequency of collisions between the particles and the syringe walls increases, giving a larger total force on a smaller surface area
examiner_note: Figure 12 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A fire piston is a special type of syringe that can be used to start fires. The plunger is pushed quickly downwards and compresses the air. When the air is compressed quickly, the temperature of the air increases.

How does an increase in temperature affect the air particles inside the piston? Tick one box.

  • The mean kinetic energy of the particles increases.
  • The mean potential energy of the particles increases.
  • The mean separation of the particles increases.
answer: The mean kinetic energy of the particles increases
examiner_note: Figure 13 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
When the air is hot enough, a small piece of cotton wool in the piston catches fire. The energy transferred to the air in the piston is 0.0130 J. The mass of air in the piston is 2.60 × 10⁻⁸ kg.

specific heat capacity of air = 1.01 kJ/kg °C

Calculate the temperature change of the air.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A teacher investigated the radiation emitted by two different radioactive sources, A and B, measuring the count rate at different distances for each source. Figure 15 shows the results.

Explain how Figure 15 shows that Source A only emits alpha radiation.
answer: Radiation from Source A travels about 3 cm in air, after which the count rate falls to the background level, because alpha radiation has a short range in air
examiner_note: Figures 14 and 15 are artwork in the PDF and are not transcribed. The 3 cm is the mark scheme's own reading of Figure 15.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Figure 15 can not be used to determine if Source B emits beta radiation or gamma radiation. Explain how an absorbing material could be used to show which type of radiation is emitted by Source B.
answer: Use an aluminium sheet, which beta radiation will not penetrate but gamma will — so only gamma gets through

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The teacher took safety precautions during the experiment. Suggest one safety precaution the teacher would have taken to reduce the radiation dose the teacher received.
answer: Any one of: increase the distance between source and teacher; limit the exposure time; use tongs or forceps; wear a lead apron; keep the source in a box unless in use; stand behind a safety screen; point the source away

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Suggest one safety precaution that the teacher would have taken to avoid becoming contaminated.
answer: Wear gloves, an apron or a lab coat, or handle the source with tongs or forceps

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 16 shows how the number of atoms of a radioactive element in a sample varied with time. Activity is the rate at which a source of unstable nuclei decays.

Determine the activity of the radioactive sample at 300 seconds. Give the unit.
answer: 7.1 × 10²⁰ becquerel (Bq) — anything from 6.5 to 7.6 × 10²⁰ is accepted. Draw a tangent to the curve at 300 s and find its gradient.
examiner_note: Figure 16 is a graph in the PDF and is not transcribed. The value is the mark scheme's own.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The live wire in a three-core cable is connected to a fuse inside a plug. A fuse contains a wire that is designed to melt when the current gets too great.

What colour is the insulation covering the live wire in a three-core cable?
answer: Brown

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Draw the circuit symbol for a fuse in the box below.
answer: A rectangle with a horizontal line drawn through it, the line continuing out of both ends
examiner_note: The symbol was read off a render of the mark scheme.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: The fuse wire melts when there is a charge flow of 2.0 C for 400 ms. Calculate the current in the fuse wire.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
When the fuse wire is at its melting point, the additional energy needed to melt the wire is 1.02 J.

specific latent heat of fuse wire = 60 kJ/kg

Calculate the mass of the fuse wire.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The calculation in Question 10.4 assumes there is no energy transferred to the surroundings. How would the time taken for the wire to melt be affected if some energy was transferred to the surroundings? Give a reason for your answer. Tick one box.

  • Time taken would decrease
  • Time taken would stay the same
  • Time taken would increase
answer: Time taken would increase, because more energy would need to be transferred in total

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the refraction of light by a glass block. Figure 1 shows the protractor used to measure the angles of incidence and the angles of refraction. It is an ordinary semicircular protractor, marked in single degrees with a double scale running 0 to 180 in both directions.

What is the resolution of the protractor used to measure the angles?

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Table 1 shows the results.

Angle of incidence in degreesAngle of refraction in degrees
106
2012
3018
4023
5028
6032

Describe a method the student could have used to obtain the data in Table 1. You may include a labelled diagram.
answer: Level-marked out of 6. Place the glass block on a piece of paper and draw around it. Shine a ray from a ray box through the block. Mark the ray going in and the ray coming out, and join the marks to show the whole path through the block. Draw a normal at 90° to the surface. Measure the angle of incidence and the angle of refraction with a protractor. Repeat over a range of angles of incidence — 10° to 60° in 10° steps. Methods using mirrors and reflection score zero.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 2 shows some of the results from Table 1. The student measured the angles of refraction for two additional angles of incidence. Table 2 shows the additional results.

Angle of incidence in degreesAngle of refraction in degrees
7035
8037

Complete Figure 2. You should:

  • plot the results from Table 2
  • draw the line of best fit.
answer: Plot (70, 35) and (80, 37) — both within half a small square — and draw a curve through all eight points. A line starting at the origin is allowed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: How does Figure 2 show that the angle of refraction is not directly proportional to the angle of incidence?
answer: The line curves — it is not straight

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 3 shows a diagram of a car headlight, which has a lamp, a curved reflective surface behind it and a flat transparent cover across the front. Figure 4 shows a ray of light leaving the lamp and meeting the curved reflective surface.

Complete Figure 4 to show the reflected ray of light. You should include the normal line at the point where the incident ray meets the reflecting surface.
answer: Draw the normal at the point where the ray meets the mirror, then the reflected ray so that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. Judged by eye.
examiner_note: Figures 3 and 4 are artwork in the PDF and are not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Rays of light pass through the transparent cover of the headlight.

Which diagram shows how a ray of light passes through the transparent cover? Tick one box.

  • The ray bends at both surfaces of the cover and leaves parallel to, but shifted sideways from, the ray that went in.
  • The ray bends at the first surface and then turns back downwards on leaving.
  • The ray passes straight through without changing direction.
answer: The first one — the ray refracts at both surfaces and emerges parallel to the incident ray but displaced sideways
examiner_note: The three diagrams are artwork in the PDF. The answer was read off a render of the mark scheme, which prints the correct one.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 5 shows a young child using a baby walker. The child is standing still.

What is the resultant vertical force on the child? Give a reason for your answer.
answer: 0 N, because the child is not accelerating vertically — the upward forces equal the downward forces, so the forces are balanced
examiner_note: Figure 5 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Write down the equation which links distance (s), force (F) and work done (W).
answer: work done = force × distance, or W = F × s

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The child pushed the baby walker 2.8 m across a horizontal floor. The work done by the child was 35 J.

Calculate the horizontal force the child applied to the baby walker.
answer: 12.5 N (13 N is also accepted)

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The child pushed the baby walker from a carpet onto a hard floor. The child applied the same horizontal force to the baby walker.

Explain why the speed of the baby walker increased.
answer: The resistive force — the friction between the wheels and the floor — has decreased, so the resultant force increases

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Write down the equation which links distance (d), force (F) and moment of a force (M).
answer: moment = force × distance, or M = F × d

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
There are some toy gears on the front of the baby walker; Figure 6 shows two of them, gear A and gear B, meshed together. The child applies a force to gear A, which causes a moment about the pivot, so gear A rotates.

The child applies a force of 2.0 N on gear A. The perpendicular distance between the force and the pivot is 7.5 cm.

Calculate the moment of the force about the pivot.
answer: 0.15 N m — convert 7.5 cm to 0.075 m first, then M = 2.0 × 0.075
examiner_note: Figure 6 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain what happens to gear B when the child applies the force to gear A.
answer: Gear B rotates in the opposite direction to gear A — or clockwise, or faster than gear A — because gear A exerts a force on gear B, causing a moment about gear B's pivot
examiner_note: Figure 6 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The Universe contains many stars. The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

Give three other types of object that form our solar system.
answer: Any three of: planets; dwarf planets; moons (natural satellites); asteroids; meteors, meteoroids or meteorites; comets

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Some main sequence stars will eventually form black holes. Table 3 gives the mass of four stars.

StarMass in kg
Arcturus2.2 × 1030
Betelgeuse2.2 × 1031
Cygni A1.4 × 1030
The Sun2.0 × 1030

Which star in Table 3 is most likely to form a black hole?
answer: Betelgeuse

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The distance from Cygni A to the Earth is 1.1 × 108 gigametres.

Which distance is the same as 1.1 × 108 gigametres? Tick one box.

  • 1.1 × 1011 m
  • 1.1 × 1014 m
  • 1.1 × 1017 m
  • 1.1 × 1020 m

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The light spectrum from every galaxy includes dark lines. The lines have the same pattern. Figure 7 shows the position of dark lines in the visible spectra of light from the Sun and from two distant galaxies.

Explain what these light spectra tell us about the velocities of galaxy A and galaxy B.
answer: Both show red-shift — the wavelength of the absorption lines has increased — so both galaxies are moving away from us. A shows a greater red-shift than B, so A is travelling faster than B.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The distance between Arcturus and the Earth is 3.6 × 1014 km.

speed of light = 3.0 × 108 m/s

Calculate the time taken for light from Arcturus to reach the Earth. Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
answer: 1.2 × 10^9 s (1 200 000 000 s) — convert the distance to 3.6 × 10^17 m first

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
When stars are formed, they contain mostly hydrogen.

Describe how stars produce all other naturally occurring elements.
answer: Level-marked out of 4. Fusion occurs at high temperatures and produces new elements. Hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium nuclei. When hydrogen in the core begins to run out, helium nuclei fuse to make heavier elements, up to iron. Some massive stars become supernovae, creating the elements heavier than iron.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The Mariana Trench is the deepest part of the Pacific Ocean. Figure 8 shows a submarine going down to the bottom of it.

The depth of the submarine increases. Explain what happens to the pressure on the submarine.
answer: The height of the column of water above the submarine increases, which increases the weight of water acting on it, so the pressure increases. (Or: p = ρgh, and ρ and g stay the same, so pressure increases.)
examiner_note: Figure 8 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The submarine moved from the surface of the water to the bottom of the Mariana Trench. The change in pressure was 110 000 kPa.

mean density of sea water = 1026 kg/m3
gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg

Calculate the depth of the Mariana Trench. Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
answer: 10 940 m (11 000 m is accepted with working) — convert 110 000 kPa to 110 000 000 Pa first

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Earthquakes often occur at the Mariana Trench. P-waves and S-waves are produced by earthquakes.

Which statement describes P-waves and S-waves? Tick one box.

  • Both P-waves and S-waves are longitudinal.
  • Both P-waves and S-waves are transverse.
  • P-waves are longitudinal and S-waves are transverse.
  • P-waves are transverse and S-waves are longitudinal.
answer: P-waves are longitudinal and S-waves are transverse

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 shows the layers inside the Earth. An earthquake occurs at the position shown.

Which letter shows the position where only P-waves will be detected? Give a reason for your answer. Tick one box: A, B, C or D.
answer: D — because only P-waves can travel through liquids, so only they get through the liquid outer core. (S-waves cannot travel through the outer core.)

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
An S-wave has a frequency of 3.6 Hz. The S-wave has a speed of 4.5 km/s.

Calculate the wavelength of this S-wave. Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
answer: 1250 m (1300 m accepted) — convert 4.5 km/s to 4500 m/s first

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A seismometer is a device that detects earthquakes. P-waves travel at a known speed between an earthquake and a seismometer. S-waves travel at a slower speed than P-waves. A P-wave and an S-wave from the earthquake arrive at the seismometer at different times.

Describe the relationship between the distance from the earthquake to the seismometer and the time between the P-wave and the S-wave arriving.
answer: The distance is directly proportional to the time between the two waves arriving. (A greater distance means a greater time, or a positive correlation, scores 1 of the 2.)

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated how the acceleration of a trolley varies with the resultant force on the trolley. Figure 10 shows some of the equipment used: a trolley on a horizontal runway, pulled by a string that runs over a pulley at the end of the bench to a hanging mass. Figure 10 shows the force F which acts through the string.

What name is given to force F?
answer: Tension
examiner_note: Figure 10 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Give one variable that should have been a control variable in this investigation.
answer: The combined mass of the trolley and the mass hanger (the mass or weight of the trolley, or of the hanger, is accepted)

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The student held the trolley stationary and then released it. The trolley moved along the runway with a constant acceleration. The student recorded the time taken for the trolley to travel a measured distance along the runway.

Describe how the acceleration of the trolley can be calculated using the time taken and distance travelled by the trolley.
answer: Divide the distance travelled by the time taken to give the mean velocity. Double the mean velocity to give the maximum velocity. Divide the change in velocity by the time taken to give the acceleration. (Using v² = u² + 2as, or s = ut + ½at², is also accepted.)

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
For one set of results, the force acting through the string was 2.0 N. The student released the trolley three times and determined the following values for acceleration:

1.36 m/s2   1.39 m/s2   1.33 m/s2

Calculate the uncertainty in the values of acceleration.
answer: ± 0.03 m/s² — the range is 0.06 m/s² (the mean is 1.36 m/s²), and the uncertainty is half the range

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The runway was then raised at one end. The force acting through the string remained the same. Figure 11 shows this.

Explain how the acceleration was affected by raising the end of the runway.
answer: A component of the weight of the trolley now acts parallel to the runway, so the resultant force increases and the acceleration increases. (Also accepted: work is done raising the trolley so it gains gravitational potential energy, which is transferred to kinetic energy, increasing the final velocity and the acceleration.)
examiner_note: Figure 11 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Radio waves and gamma rays both transfer energy.

Give three other similarities between radio waves and gamma rays.
answer: Any three of: they travel at the same speed in a vacuum (the speed of light); they can travel through a vacuum (they need no medium); they are transverse waves; they are electromagnetic waves. Being reflected, refracted, absorbed, transmitted or diffracted is ignored.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Both radio waves and gamma rays are used in medicine.

Give one medical use of gamma rays.
answer: Medical imaging — a PET scan, a tracer or a gamma camera — or a medical treatment such as radiotherapy or a gamma knife. Sterilising medical equipment is also accepted. Ultrasound, CT, X-rays, MRI and chemotherapy are not.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain why exposure to gamma rays can be harmful but exposure to radio waves is not harmful.
answer: Gamma rays are ionising and radio waves are not, so gamma rays can cause mutations in genes or DNA — increasing the risk of cancer, or damaging and killing cells

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Some medical scanners produce radio waves at a specific frequency.

Explain how radio waves are produced at a specific frequency.
answer: Radio waves are produced by oscillations in the electrical circuits of the scanner — an alternating current, or oscillating electrons in an aerial — and the radio waves have the same frequency as those oscillations

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 12 shows a velocity–time graph for a train travelling between two stations.

Determine the distance travelled by the train in the first 600 s of the journey.
answer: 27 440 m — the triangle is ½ × 56 × 220 = 6160 m and the rectangle is 56 × 380 = 21 280 m

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain what happens to the braking force as the train decelerates. Use information from Figure 12.
answer: The gradient is less after 720 s (after the velocity has fallen to 20 m/s), so the deceleration is smaller, so the braking force is smaller

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Determine the maximum deceleration of the train.
answer: 0.3 m/s² — the steepest section is from 600 s to 720 s, where the gradient is −36 ÷ 120

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Another train travels at a speed of 60 m/s. A constant braking force of 270 000 N causes the train to decelerate and stop.

mass of train = 240 000 kg

Calculate the distance travelled while the braking force is applied. Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
answer: 1600 m. By forces: a = −270 000 ÷ 240 000 = −1.125 m/s², then 0 = 60² + 2(−1.125)s, so s = 3600 ÷ 2.25. By energy: Ek = ½ × 240 000 × 60² = 432 000 000 J, which equals the work done, so s = 432 000 000 ÷ 270 000. By momentum: p = 14 400 000 kg m/s, t = 53.3 s, mean speed 30 m/s, s = 30 × 53.3.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
It is illegal for train drivers to drink alcohol before driving a train.

Explain how drinking alcohol would affect the stopping distance of a train.
answer: Stopping distance is braking distance plus thinking distance. Alcohol increases the driver's reaction time, which increases the thinking distance, so the stopping distance increases.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 13 shows some apparatus used by a teacher in a demonstration: a length of wire held between the poles of two magnets, with its ends connected to an ammeter. The teacher moved the wire upwards between the magnets. The needle on the ammeter deflected to a value of +0.4 mA and then returned to zero.

What effect did this demonstrate?
answer: The generator effect (electromagnetic induction)
examiner_note: Figure 13 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain why a current was detected when the wire in Figure 13 was moved upwards.
answer: The wire cuts through the magnetic field between the magnets, so a potential difference is induced across the wire, and as the wire is part of a complete circuit there is a current in the circuit
examiner_note: Figure 13 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The teacher reversed the direction of the magnetic field, replaced the wire in its original position, and moved the wire upwards in the same way as before.

What was the deflection of the needle on the ammeter? Tick one box.

  • The needle will deflect to −0.4 mA.
  • The needle will not move.
  • The needle will deflect to +0.4 mA.
answer: The needle will deflect to −0.4 mA

subject: Physics
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 14 shows a sound wave incident on the diaphragm of a moving-coil microphone. The inside of the microphone includes a small coil of wire and a magnet.

Explain why the sound waves have an effect on the electric circuit.
answer: The pressure variations in the sound waves cause the diaphragm to vibrate; the diaphragm causes the coil to vibrate; and as the coil repeatedly changes direction it induces an alternating current in the circuit.
examiner_note: Figure 14 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student produced a salt by reacting copper carbonate with sulfuric acid. This is the method used.

  1. Measure 50 cm3 of sulfuric acid into a beaker.
  2. Add copper carbonate powder.
  3. Stir the mixture.
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 until copper carbonate is in excess.
  5. Filter the mixture.
  6. Warm the filtrate gently until crystals start to appear.
  7. Leave the solution to cool and crystallise.

Complete the word equation for the reaction.

copper carbonate + sulfuric acid → ............... + ............... + carbon dioxide
answer: copper sulfate + water (CuSO₄ and H₂O are accepted)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give one observation the student could make during Step 4 which shows that the copper carbonate is in excess.
answer: Solid remains in the mixture — or there is no more effervescence, bubbling or fizzing

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give one reason for filtering the mixture in Step 5.
answer: To remove the excess copper carbonate

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Name the equipment that can be used to warm the filtrate gently in Step 6.
answer: An electric heater, or a water bath. (A Bunsen burner is ignored.)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The maximum theoretical mass of the salt that could be produced using 50 cm3 of the sulfuric acid is 12.5 g. The percentage yield of the salt is 92.8%.

Calculate the mass of salt actually produced. Use the equation:

% yield = (mass of salt actually produced ÷ maximum theoretical mass of salt that could be produced) × 100

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Some salts can be produced by reacting sulfuric acid with a metal. Neither copper nor sodium is used to produce a salt with sulfuric acid.

Give one reason why each metal is not used.
answer: Copper: it does not react with the acid — it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it will not displace hydrogen. Sodium: the reaction is dangerous — it could explode, or get too hot.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about the periodic table. Sodium and potassium are in Group 1 of the periodic table.

Give one similarity and one difference between the electronic structures of sodium and potassium.
answer: Similarity: both have one electron in their outer shell. Difference: sodium has 3 shells and potassium has 4.
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Group 1 elements react with water.

Give two observations made when potassium reacts with water.
answer: Any two of: effervescence, bubbling or fizzing; the potassium floats; it moves around; it gets smaller; it melts or forms a ball; a flame; an explosion

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Potassium hydroxide solution is produced when potassium reacts with water.

What is the colour of universal indicator when added to potassium hydroxide solution? Give one reason for your answer.
answer: Blue, violet or purple — because the solution is alkaline (it contains hydroxide, OH⁻, ions)
