subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The elements in Group 7 are called the halogens. A more reactive halogen can displace a less reactive halogen from a solution of its salt.

Which combination of solutions will produce a reaction when mixed? Tick one box.

  • Chlorine and potassium fluoride
  • Chlorine and potassium bromide
  • Bromine and potassium fluoride
  • Bromine and potassium chloride
answer: Chlorine and potassium bromide
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which of the following describes the trends going down Group 7? Tick one box.

  • Relative molecular mass decreases and boiling point decreases.
  • Relative molecular mass decreases and boiling point increases.
  • Relative molecular mass increases and boiling point decreases.
  • Relative molecular mass increases and boiling point increases.
answer: Relative molecular mass increases and boiling point increases
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about models of the atom. Figure 2 shows two early models of the atom. Model A is a shaded ball of positive charge with four electrons dotted about inside it. Model B is a small positive nucleus at the centre with electrons arranged on two circular shells around it.

Name the models of the atom shown in Figure 2.
answer: Model A: the plum pudding model (Thomson). Model B: the Bohr model (also accepted: nuclear, planetary, Rutherford-Bohr).
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table
examiner_note: Figure 2 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Compare model A with the model of the atom used today. Use Figure 2.
answer: Level-marked out of 4. Similarities: both contain electrons; both are neutral overall. Differences: model A has no nucleus, no protons and no neutrons, where today's model has all three. In model A the positive charge and the mass are spread throughout the atom; today the positive charge and almost all the mass are concentrated in the centre. In model A the electrons are distributed randomly; today they are in shells or energy levels. Model A has no empty space; today's atom is mostly empty space.
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table
examiner_note: Figure 2 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Chadwick's experiments showed the existence of neutrons in an atom. This led to an understanding of isotopes.

Define the term 'isotopes'. Refer to subatomic particles in your answer.
answer: Atoms with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the energy change of the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution. This is the method used.

  1. Measure 25 cm3 of copper sulfate solution into a polystyrene cup.
  2. Measure the temperature of the copper sulfate solution.
  3. Add 0.20 g of zinc powder to the copper sulfate solution.
  4. Stir the reaction mixture.
  5. Record the highest temperature reached.
  6. Repeat steps 1 to 5 with different masses of zinc powder.

Figure 3 shows the results.

Draw two lines of best fit on Figure 3. The lines should cross.
answer: One line of best fit through the first five points (the rising part), and a second through the last four (the flat part). Maximum 1 mark if the lines do not intersect.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Explain the results shown in Figure 3. Do not refer to anomalous points. Use data from Figure 3.
answer: The temperature rises because the reaction is exothermic — energy is transferred to the surroundings — until 0.8 g of zinc is added (where the temperature reaches 47 °C). After that there is no additional reaction, because the zinc is in excess and the copper sulfate has been used up.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Explain why using a polystyrene cup gives more accurate results than using a glass beaker.
answer: Polystyrene is a better thermal insulator, so less energy is transferred to the surroundings

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Complete the ionic equation for the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution. Include state symbols.

Zn(s) + Cu2+(aq) → ............... + ...............
answer: Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s). Zn²⁺ and Cu without state symbols scores 1 of the 2.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A different student repeated steps 1 to 5 of the method four times using 0.50 g of zinc powder. Table 2 shows the results.

Trial 1Trial 2Trial 3Trial 4
Highest temperature reached in °C37.637.237.837.4

Calculate the mean highest temperature reached. Include the uncertainty in your answer.
answer: 37.5 ± 0.3 °C — the mean is (37.6 + 37.2 + 37.8 + 37.4) ÷ 4 = 150 ÷ 4, and the uncertainty is half the range of 0.6 °C

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The results show random errors. The student did not make any measuring errors.

Suggest one reason for the random errors in this experiment.
answer: The starting temperature may have been different each time, or the stirring was inconsistent (or the lid was used inconsistently)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about ionic compounds and electrolysis. Calcium chloride is an ionic compound. Calcium and chlorine react to produce calcium chloride.

Describe what happens to calcium atoms and chlorine atoms when the ionic compound calcium chloride is formed.
answer: Each calcium atom loses two electrons and each chlorine atom gains one electron, so one calcium atom reacts with two chlorine atoms, forming Ca²⁺ ions and Cl⁻ ions — all with full outer shells. Just 'calcium atoms lose electrons and chlorine atoms gain electrons' scores 1 of the 4.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Solid calcium chloride cannot be electrolysed. Give one reason why.
answer: The ions cannot move — they are in fixed positions

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Name the product formed at the negative electrode when aqueous calcium chloride solution is electrolysed.
answer: Hydrogen

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the half equation for the reaction at the positive electrode when aqueous calcium chloride solution is electrolysed? Tick one box.

  • 2 Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2 e⁻
  • Cl₂ + 2 e⁻ → 2 Cl⁻
  • 4 OH⁻ → O₂ + 2 H₂O + 4 e⁻
  • O₂ + 2 H₂O + 4 e⁻ → 4 OH⁻
answer: 2 Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2 e⁻

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the electrolysis of green copper chromate solution. Figure 4 shows the apparatus: a piece of filter paper soaked in an electrolyte solution lies between a negative electrode on the left and a positive electrode on the right, with a drop of green copper chromate solution in the middle and a power supply across the two electrodes.

Figure 5 shows the results. The green drop has separated into two patches: a blue patch on the side nearer the negative electrode and a yellow patch on the side nearer the positive electrode.

Copper chromate solution contains the ions Cu2+ and CrO42−.

Explain the results shown in Figure 5.
answer: Cu²⁺ (copper) ions are blue and CrO₄²⁻ (chromate) ions are yellow. The Cu²⁺ ions move towards the negative electrode, and the CrO₄²⁻ ions move towards the positive electrode.
examiner_note: Figures 4 and 5 are artwork in the PDF and are not transcribed; what each shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the voltage produced by different pairs of metal electrodes in a chemical cell. Figure 6 shows the apparatus: two metal electrodes standing in a beaker of solution, connected to a voltmeter. This is the method used.

  1. Place a nickel electrode and an electrode made from a different metal (electrode A) in 1.0 mol/dm3 sodium chloride solution.
  2. Measure the voltage produced.
  3. Repeat using different metals for electrode A.

Table 3 shows the results.

Electrode ASymbol of metalVoltage in volts
CopperCu−0.59
MagnesiumMg2.12
NickelNi0.00
SilverAg−1.05
ZincZn0.51

Write the symbols of the five metals in Table 3 in order of reactivity, most reactive first. Justify your answer.
answer: Mg, Zn, Ni, Cu, Ag. Justification: the higher the positive voltage, the more reactive the metal. Getting either Mg, Zn, Ni or Ni, Cu, Ag in the right order scores 1 of the 2 order marks.
examiner_note: Figure 6 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The voltage produced by a chemical cell depends on the concentration of the electrolyte solution.

Plan an experiment to investigate how the voltage produced by a chemical cell varies with the concentration of the electrolyte solution. The following substances are available:

  • the metal electrodes in Table 3
  • 1.0 mol/dm3 sodium chloride solution
  • pure water.
answer: Level-marked out of 6. Set up a cell with sodium chloride solution as the electrolyte and two different metals as the electrodes. Measure the voltage. Repeat at different concentrations, made by diluting the sodium chloride solution with pure water, using measured volumes of each — a measuring cylinder, pipette or burette. Use the same two metals and the same volume of electrolyte every time.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Describe how a hydrogen fuel cell produces a potential difference.
answer: Hydrogen is oxidised electrochemically — it loses electrons — to produce water

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about iron. Iron is a metal.

Describe how iron conducts thermal energy.
answer: Thermal energy is transferred by the delocalised electrons

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Pure iron is too soft for many uses.

Explain why mixing iron with other metals makes alloys which are harder than pure iron.
answer: The alloy contains atoms of different sizes, so the layers are distorted, so the layers cannot easily slide over each other

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
When iron reacts with chlorine, 0.12 mol of iron reacts with 0.18 mol of chlorine (Cl2).

Which is the correct equation for the reaction? Tick one box.

  • Fe + Cl₂ → FeCl₂
  • Fe + 3 Cl₂ → FeCl₆
  • 2 Fe + Cl₂ → 2 FeCl
  • 2 Fe + 3 Cl₂ → 2 FeCl₃
answer: 2 Fe + 3 Cl₂ → 2 FeCl₃ — the ratio 0.12 : 0.18 is 2 : 3

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The most common oxides of iron are Fe2O3 and Fe3O4.

What is the ratio of the numbers of ions in Fe3O4? Tick one box.

  • 2 Fe²⁺ : 1 Fe³⁺ : 4 O²⁻
  • 1 Fe²⁺ : 2 Fe³⁺ : 4 O²⁻
  • 3 Fe²⁺ : 4 O²⁻
  • 3 Fe³⁺ : 4 O²⁻
answer: 1 Fe²⁺ : 2 Fe³⁺ : 4 O²⁻

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Calculate the percentage (%) by mass of iron in Fe3O4.

Relative atomic masses (Ar): O = 16, Fe = 56

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Fe2O3 reacts with carbon to produce carbon dioxide. The equation for the reaction is:

2 Fe2O3(s) + 3 C(s) → 4 Fe(s) + 3 CO2(g)

Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide gas at room temperature and pressure that is produced from 40.0 kg of Fe2O3 using excess carbon.

Relative formula mass (Mr): Fe2O3 = 160
The volume of 1 mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is 24 dm3.
answer: 9000 dm³ — 40.0 kg is 40 000 g, which is 40 000 ÷ 160 = 250 mol of Fe₂O₃; that gives 250 × 3/2 = 375 mol of CO₂; and 375 × 24 = 9000 dm³

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about propane (C3H8). Figure 7 shows its displayed structural formula: a chain of three carbon atoms, each joined to the next by a single bond, with hydrogen atoms filling every remaining bond — three on each end carbon and two on the middle one.

Explain why propane has a low boiling point.
answer: Propane is a small (simple) molecule, so the intermolecular forces between the molecules are weak, so little energy is needed to overcome them. Not the covalent bonds — those are not broken when propane boils.
examiner_note: Figure 7 is artwork in the PDF; the structure is described rather than drawn.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Propane reacts with oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water. The reaction is exothermic.

Figure 8 shows four reaction profiles. All four have energy up the side and progress of reaction along the bottom, and all four are labelled 'overall energy change' beside an arrow between the reactant level and the product level.

  • A — products lower than reactants, arrow pointing up
  • B — products lower than reactants, arrow pointing down
  • C — products higher than reactants, arrow pointing down
  • D — products higher than reactants, arrow pointing up

Which is the correct reaction profile and labels for the reaction between propane and oxygen? Tick one box.
answer: B — the products are lower in energy than the reactants because the reaction is exothermic, and the arrow points downwards from the reactant level to the product level
examiner_note: Figure 8 is artwork in the PDF; what each of the four profiles shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 shows the displayed formula equation for the reaction between propane and oxygen:

C3H8 + 5 O=O → 3 O=C=O + 4 H—O—H

The overall energy change of this exothermic reaction is 2219 kJ/mol. Table 4 shows the bond energies of the bonds in the reaction.

BondC — CC — HO = OC = OO — H
Energy in kJ/mol347X498805464

Calculate the bond energy of the C — H bond (X).
answer: 392 kJ/mol. Bonds broken = 2(347) + 8X + 5(498) = 3184 + 8X. Bonds made = 6(805) + 8(464) = 8542. Energy released = bonds made − bonds broken, so 2219 = 8542 − (3184 + 8X), giving 8X = 3139 and X = 392.375.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about acids and their reactions. Acids can be either weak or strong.

What is meant by 'a weak acid'?
answer: An acid which is only partially ionised (partially dissociated) in aqueous solution

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Explain what happens to the pH of an acid as the acid is diluted with water.
answer: The pH increases, because the concentration of hydrogen ions decreases

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student does a titration to find the volume of acid needed to neutralise an alkali. The student fills a burette with the acid.

Give three more steps the student must do before adding the acid to the alkali from the burette. You should name any equipment used.
answer: Use a volumetric pipette to add the alkali (this mark is compulsory), then any two of: into a conical flask; add an indicator to the alkali; take the initial burette reading; stand the flask on a white tile. Universal indicator is not accepted.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The student titrated a solution containing 0.0045 moles of sodium hydroxide with 0.15 mol/dm3 hydrochloric acid. The equation for the reaction is:

NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O

Calculate the volume of hydrochloric acid in cm3 needed in the titration.
answer: 30 cm³ — 0.0045 ÷ 0.15 = 0.030 dm³, which is 30 cm³

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A calcium atom is larger than a magnesium atom.

Explain why calcium reacts more vigorously than magnesium with hydrochloric acid of the same concentration.
answer: Calcium's outer electrons are further from the nucleus (it has more shells, so they are more shielded), so they are less strongly attracted to the nucleus, so positive ions are formed more easily — the electrons are more easily lost
topics: Atomic Structure and the Periodic Table

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated an aqueous solution of a salt. The student identified that the salt solution contained only sodium ions and chloride ions.

Describe a test to identify sodium ions. Give the result of the test.
answer: Test: a flame test. Result: a yellow flame. (Or: flame emission spectroscopy, and the lines match the sodium spectrum.)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe a test to identify chloride ions. Give the result of the test.
answer: Test: add acidified silver nitrate solution. Result: a white precipitate. The result mark depends on getting the test right.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The student determined the concentration of sodium chloride in the salt solution. This is the method used.

  1. Weigh an empty evaporating dish.
  2. Add 25.0 cm3 of the salt solution into the evaporating dish.
  3. Heat the evaporating dish and contents.
  4. Weigh the evaporating dish and contents.
  5. Repeat steps 3 to 4 until there is no further change in mass.
  6. Repeat steps 1 to 5 three more times.

Why did the student heat the evaporating dish and contents until the mass did not change?
answer: To make sure all the water had evaporated

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
How did the student calculate the mass of solid sodium chloride remaining after steps 1 to 5? Tick one box.

  • Mass of 25 cm3 of salt solution + mass of empty evaporating dish
  • Mass of 25 cm3 of salt solution − mass of empty evaporating dish
  • Mass of evaporating dish and dry contents + mass of empty evaporating dish
  • Mass of evaporating dish and dry contents − mass of empty evaporating dish
answer: Mass of evaporating dish and dry contents − mass of empty evaporating dish

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The student calculated the concentration of sodium chloride in the salt solution. Table 1 shows the results.

Concentration of sodium chloride in g/dm3Trial 1Trial 2Trial 3Trial 4
35.234.636.433.8

The percentage by mass of sodium ions in sodium chloride is 39.3%.

Calculate the mean concentration of sodium ions in the salt solution.
answer: 13.8 g/dm³. The mean concentration of sodium chloride is (35.2 + 34.6 + 36.4 + 33.8) ÷ 4 = 140 ÷ 4 = 35.0 g/dm³, and 35.0 × 39.3 ÷ 100 = 13.755, which rounds to 13.8.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This question is about ammonia and nitric acid. In the Haber process ammonia is produced from nitrogen and hydrogen. Figure 1 is a flow diagram of the process: nitrogen and hydrogen enter a reactor, the mixture leaves it and passes through a condenser where liquid ammonia is drawn off, and a pipe P runs from the condenser back to the reactor.

Pipe P links the condenser to the reactor. Why is the condenser linked to the reactor? Use Figure 1.
answer: To recycle the unreacted nitrogen and hydrogen back into the reactor
examiner_note: Figure 1 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Which metal is used as a catalyst in this reaction?
answer: Iron

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Nitric acid is produced by reacting ammonia with oxygen. The word equation is:

ammonia + oxygen → water + nitric acid

Platinum is a catalyst in this reaction.

Describe the test for oxygen gas. Give the result if oxygen gas is present.
answer: Test: put a glowing splint into the gas. Result: the splint relights. The result mark depends on getting the test right.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 2 represents the reaction profile of the catalysed reaction between ammonia and oxygen: energy up the side, progress of reaction along the bottom, a curve that starts at a dotted reactant level, rises to a peak and falls to a lower product level. Nothing on it is labelled.

Complete the reaction profile for the catalysed reaction in Figure 2. You should:

  • label the activation energy
  • label the reactants and products, using the names of the reactants and products.
answer: Draw a labelled vertical arrow from the dotted reactant line up to the peak — that is the activation energy. Label the left-hand level 'ammonia and oxygen' and the right-hand level 'nitric acid and water' (formulae are accepted).
examiner_note: Figure 2 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
How would Figure 2 be different if no catalyst was used? Tick one box.

  • The final energy level would be higher.
  • The final energy level would be lower.
  • The line would reach a higher peak.
  • The line would reach a lower peak.
answer: The line would reach a higher peak — without a catalyst the activation energy is larger

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Ammonia and nitric acid react to produce the salt, ammonium nitrate. Ammonium ions and nitrate ions both contain nitrogen.

Suggest one use of ammonium nitrate.
answer: Fertiliser (explosives and sports injury packs are also accepted)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This question is about water. Hydrogen gas reacts with oxygen gas to produce water. Water is decomposed into hydrogen gas and oxygen gas using electricity.

Which two words describe the reaction between hydrogen gas and oxygen gas? Tick two boxes.

  • Alloying
  • Combustion
  • Corrosion
  • Endothermic
  • Reversible
answer: Combustion and reversible

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Water molecules break down into hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions. The equation for the reaction is:

H2O ⇌ H+ + OH−

Which sentence describes this reaction at equilibrium? Tick one box.

  • Water molecules break down at a higher rate than they reform.
  • Water molecules break down and reform at the same rate.
  • Water molecules break down at a lower rate than they reform.
answer: Water molecules break down and reform at the same rate

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Water collected from rivers is used in the home for drinking and flushing toilets. Water used in the home must be potable — safe to drink. Waste water produced after use in the home is called sewage.

Figure 3 is a flow diagram: water is taken from a river and goes through Process A before reaching the home, and the sewage leaving the home goes through Process B before returning to the river.

Explain what happens to water in Process A and in Process B. Do not refer to use of water in the home.
answer: Level-marked out of 6, and Level 3 needs both halves. Process A — making water potable: pass the water through filter beds to remove solids, then sterilise it with chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light to destroy microbes. Process B — treating waste water: screening through a metal grid to remove solids and grit, then sedimentation to separate sewage sludge from effluent, then anaerobic digestion of the sludge and aerobic biological treatment of the effluent.
examiner_note: Figure 3 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated an orange dye (A) using paper chromatography. Figure 4 shows two chromatography beakers side by side. In Experiment 1 the solvent is water; the paper carries a start line near the bottom, a yellow spot about halfway up and a red spot below it, with the solvent front near the top. In Experiment 2 the solvent is ethanol; the red spot is in much the same place, but the yellow spot has travelled noticeably further — it now sits just under the solvent front.

Explain why the yellow dye and red dye travel different distances in Experiment 1. Refer to forces of attraction between the dyes and the chromatography paper in your answer.
answer: The yellow dye travels further because it has a weaker attraction to the chromatography paper (the stationary phase). 'The weaker the attraction to the paper, the further the dye travels' alone scores 1 of the 2.
examiner_note: Figure 4 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 4 shows two chromatography beakers side by side. In Experiment 1 the solvent is water; the paper carries a start line near the bottom, a yellow spot about halfway up and a red spot below it, with the solvent front near the top. In Experiment 2 the solvent is ethanol; the red spot is in much the same place, but the yellow spot has travelled noticeably further — it now sits just under the solvent front.

The student used the same type of chromatography paper in Experiment 1 and in Experiment 2.

Explain why the yellow dye is in different positions in Experiment 1 and in Experiment 2. Use Figure 4.
answer: In Experiment 2 the yellow dye travels further, because the solvents are different, and the yellow dye is more soluble in (more attracted to) ethanol than water.
examiner_note: Figure 4 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The student investigated a different orange dye (B). Figure 5 shows the results of Experiment 3 using orange dye B: the same apparatus, and a single spot on the paper above the start line — where dye A had separated into two.

Compare the purity of the orange dyes A and B. Give reasons for your answer. Use Figure 4 and Figure 5.
answer: A is impure (a mixture) and B is pure, because A separates into two dyes — two spots — and B produces only one.
examiner_note: Figure 5 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The student calculated that the Rf value of the orange dye in the experiment shown in Figure 5 was 0.48.

Calculate the distance moved by the solvent front when the orange dye had moved 5.4 cm.
answer: 11.25 cm — 0.48 = 5.4 ÷ distance moved by solvent, so the distance is 5.4 ÷ 0.48

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Why is the Rf value of a dye not affected by how far the solvent front is allowed to travel?
answer: Because the Rᶠ value is a ratio — the distance moved by the spot is directly proportional to the distance moved by the solvent, so the proportion stays the same

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Another type of chromatography is called gas chromatography. Gas chromatography is an instrumental method of chemical analysis. Scientists tested the orange dyes using gas chromatography.

Suggest two advantages of using the instrumental method of gas chromatography rather than paper chromatography.
answer: Any two of: it is more sensitive; it is more accurate; it is faster; it needs a smaller sample; it gives greater resolution

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This question is about burning fuels in central heating boilers.

Explain how oxides of nitrogen are produced when burning fuels.
answer: The high temperatures in the flame cause nitrogen and oxygen from the air to react together

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
In the future, gas central heating boilers may burn hydrogen rather than natural gas. Table 2 shows information about these fuels when 1 dm3 of the fuel is burned in a central heating boiler.

FuelHydrogenNatural gas
Energy released in kJ11.937.1
Mass of carbon dioxide produced in grams0.001.83
Mass of water vapour produced in grams0.751.50
Mass of oxides of nitrogen produced in grams6.6 × 10−44.9 × 10−4

Explain one positive impact on the environment of burning hydrogen rather than natural gas as a fuel. Use Table 2.
answer: Less climate change (less global warming), because burning hydrogen produces no carbon dioxide — 0.00 g against 1.83 g

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain one negative impact on the environment of burning hydrogen rather than natural gas as a fuel. Use Table 2.
answer: More oxides of nitrogen are produced — 6.6 × 10⁻⁴ g against 4.9 × 10⁻⁴ g — so more acid rain, or more respiratory problems

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Air is 20% oxygen.

Calculate the volume of air needed to provide enough oxygen to react with 3.50 dm3 of hydrogen gas. The equation for the reaction is

2 H2 + O2 → 2 H2O
answer: 8.75 dm³ — the equation needs half as much oxygen as hydrogen, so 3.50 × ½ = 1.75 dm³ of oxygen, and 1.75 × 100 ÷ 20 = 8.75 dm³ of air

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Central heating boilers can also burn kerosene. Kerosene is produced from crude oil in a fractionating column using fractional distillation. In the first step, crude oil is heated and hydrocarbon vapours are formed.

Explain how kerosene is produced from these hydrocarbon vapours.
answer: There is a temperature gradient in the fractionating column — it gets cooler going up — so the kerosene condenses at the level in the column that matches kerosene's boiling point range. Both of the last two marks need kerosene named.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This question is about materials used to make bicycles. Figure 6 is a photograph of a bicycle. Table 3 shows information about two materials used to make bicycle frames.

MaterialAluminium alloyBamboo
Raw materialaluminium orebamboo plant
Cost of frame in £2501500
Strength in arbitrary units290193
Mass in kilograms1.62.4
Lifespan in years6–1010–15
One method of disposal at end of liferecycled to make new productsburned to produce heat energy

Evaluate the use of aluminium alloy and of bamboo for making bicycle frames. Use Table 3.
answer: Level-marked out of 6, and Level 3 needs a reasoned judgement. For bamboo: it is renewable, it can be burned to give renewable heat and is carbon neutral, and the frame lasts longer (10–15 years against 6–10) — but it costs six times as much, is weaker (193 against 290), is heavier (2.4 kg against 1.6 kg) and growing it uses agricultural land. For aluminium alloy: it is cheaper, stronger, lighter — so the bicycle is faster and easier to carry — and it is recyclable, so the ore is conserved; but aluminium is a finite resource and mining the ore is polluting. Neither material need reach landfill.
examiner_note: Figure 6 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain why aluminium alloy bicycle frames do not need protection from corrosion.
answer: Aluminium alloy has an oxide coating, which stops water and oxygen reaching the aluminium underneath. (Not sacrificial protection.)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Bicycle chains are made from an alloy of iron. Bicycle chains rust without protection. Paint is not used to protect bicycle chains from rusting.

Suggest how bicycle chains can be protected from rusting.
answer: Coat them with grease or oil (galvanising, or using stainless steel, is also accepted)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Bicycle frames can also be made from a composite of carbon fibres embedded in a polymer resin.

What description is given in this composite to the carbon fibre component, and to the polymer resin component?
answer: Carbon fibre: the reinforcement. Polymer resin: the matrix (or binder).

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This question is about sulfuric acid. Sulfuric acid contains sulfate ions.

Describe the test for the presence of sulfate ions in sulfuric acid. Give the result of the test.
answer: Test: add barium chloride solution (barium nitrate is accepted). Result: a white precipitate. The result mark depends on getting the test right.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
One stage in the industrial production of sulfuric acid is the reaction of sulfur dioxide with oxygen to produce sulfur trioxide. This reversible reaction reaches dynamic equilibrium.

Figure 7 is a graph of the percentage yield of sulfur trioxide against temperature: the yield falls as the temperature rises.

Which statement about the forward reaction is correct? Use Figure 7. Tick one box.

  • The yield is greater at higher temperatures because the reaction is exothermic.
  • The yield is greater at higher temperatures because the reaction is endothermic.
  • The yield is smaller at higher temperatures because the reaction is exothermic.
  • The yield is smaller at higher temperatures because the reaction is endothermic.
answer: The yield is smaller at higher temperatures because the reaction is exothermic
examiner_note: Figure 7 is artwork in the PDF; the trend it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The equation for the reaction is:

2 SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2 SO3(g)

Explain why the percentage yield of sulfur trioxide in this reaction is greater if the pressure is higher.
answer: There are more moles of gas on the left-hand side (3 against 2), so raising the pressure shifts the position of equilibrium to the right

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
In industry, the reaction is done at 450 °C and atmospheric pressure. Under these conditions the yield of sulfur trioxide is 86%.

Suggest two reasons why a higher pressure is not used.
answer: Any two of: the yield is already high; more energy would be needed; the risk of explosion increases; the extra income from a higher yield is outweighed by the extra cost; stronger vessels and more safety precautions cost more

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This reaction uses a catalyst to increase the rate of the reaction. The catalyst is a metal oxide.

Which is the most likely metal in the metal oxide catalyst? Use the periodic table. Tick one box.

  • Aluminium (Al)
  • Barium (Ba)
  • Potassium (K)
  • Vanadium (V)
answer: Vanadium (V) — it is the only transition metal in the list

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
This question is about monomers and polymers. Compound A has an alkene functional group and an ester functional group.

Figure 8 represents a molecule of compound A, drawn as a displayed formula: a CH2=CH— group at the top, whose lower carbon is joined through an oxygen to a carbon that carries a double-bonded oxygen, and that carbon is joined to a CH3 group. Written along a line it is CH2=CH—O—C(=O)—CH3.

Draw a circle around the alkene functional group on Figure 8.
answer: Circle the C=C double bond at the top of the molecule, with the two carbons and the bond between them inside the circle
examiner_note: Figure 8 is artwork in the PDF; the structure is written out in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe what will be seen when compound A is shaken with bromine water.
answer: The orange bromine water turns colourless (is decolourised). 'Clear' is not enough.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 is a repeat of Figure 8.

Draw a circle around the ester functional group on Figure 9.
answer: Circle the —O—C(=O)— group in the middle of the molecule: the single-bonded oxygen, the carbon it joins, and that carbon's double-bonded oxygen
examiner_note: Figure 9 is artwork in the PDF; the structure is written out at 08.1.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Compound A has the formula C4H6O2. Compound A is flammable.

Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of compound A.
answer: 2 C₄H₆O₂ + 9 O₂ → 8 CO₂ + 6 H₂O (multiples are accepted). Getting the reactants right with wrong numbers, or the products right with wrong numbers, scores 1 each.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Many molecules of compound A join together to form polymer B.

Complete the displayed formula equation which represents this reaction — the monomer on the left with an n in front of it, and the repeating unit in brackets on the right.
answer: Draw the repeating unit with a SINGLE C—C bond where the monomer had the double bond — the rest of the molecule unchanged, and trailing bonds out of each end carbon with no extra atoms on them — and write n after the closing bracket.
examiner_note: The answer is a drawing in the mark scheme; it is described rather than reproduced.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
What type of polymer is polymer B? Tick one box.

  • Addition polymer
  • Condensation polymer
  • DNA
  • Protein
answer: Addition polymer

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Polymer B is a polymer which melts when heated.

What word is used to describe polymers which melt when heated?
answer: Thermosoftening (thermoplastic is accepted)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain why some polymers do not melt when heated.
answer: They have cross-links — covalent bonds — between the polymer chains, and too much energy would be needed to overcome them

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the rate of the reaction between zinc and sulfuric acid. The equation for the reaction is

Zn(s) + H2SO4(aq) → ZnSO4(aq) + H2(g)

Figure 10 shows the apparatus: a stoppered conical flask with a delivery tube running into an inverted 50 cm3 measuring cylinder standing in a trough of water. This is the method used.

  1. Pour 50 cm3 of sulfuric acid into the conical flask.
  2. Add excess zinc to the conical flask.
  3. Insert the stopper and start a timer.
  4. Measure the volume of hydrogen collected in the 50 cm3 measuring cylinder every 20 seconds for 180 seconds.

Explain why the volume of hydrogen collected in the measuring cylinder is less than the volume of hydrogen produced.
answer: Some hydrogen escapes from the flask, because the reaction starts before the stopper is put in — the stopper cannot be inserted instantly. (One mark alone: some air from the flask is collected, or some hydrogen stays in the flask or the delivery tube.)
examiner_note: Figure 10 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 11 shows the two measuring cylinders: after 40 seconds it reads 25 cm3, and after 100 seconds it reads 39 cm3.

Determine the number of moles of hydrogen collected between 40 seconds and 100 seconds. The volume of one mole of any gas at room temperature and pressure is 24 dm3.
answer: 5.8 × 10⁻⁴ mol. The volume collected is 39 − 25 = 14 cm³, which is 0.014 dm³, and 0.014 ÷ 24 = 5.8333… × 10⁻⁴.
examiner_note: Figure 11 is artwork in the PDF; the two readings are the mark scheme's own.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
A different student investigated how the concentration of sulfuric acid affected the rate of the reaction, using sulfuric acid of concentration 0.40 mol/dm3, and calculated the number of moles of hydrogen collected after every 20 seconds.

Figure 12 shows the results: moles of hydrogen collected up the side against time in seconds along the bottom. The curve climbs steeply from the origin, passes about 0.0140 mol at 50 seconds, bends over, and levels off at about 0.0168 mol from roughly 140 seconds onwards.

Determine the rate of reaction at 45 seconds. You should draw a tangent on Figure 12. Give your answer in standard form.
answer: Draw a tangent to the curve at 45 s, read a y step and an x step off it, and divide — rate = y step ÷ x step, then write the answer in standard form in mol/s. The scheme marks the tangent, the two readings, the division, the calculation and the standard form separately, and allows a correct calculation from a tangent drawn slightly differently.
examiner_note: Figure 12 is a graph in the PDF and is not transcribed; the readings quoted are off the printed curve.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Figure 13 shows the results for 0.40 mol/dm3 sulfuric acid — the same curve as Figure 12, levelling off at about 0.0168 mol.

The student repeated the experiment using 0.20 mol/dm3 sulfuric acid instead. Excess zinc was used in each experiment.

Sketch a line on Figure 13 to show the results you would expect.
answer: A line starting at the origin, less steep than the one already drawn, levelling off at 0.0084 mol — half the final value, because there is half as much acid and the zinc is in excess in both.
examiner_note: Figure 13 is a graph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Explain how increasing the temperature would affect the rate of reaction between zinc and sulfuric acid.
answer: It increases the rate, because the particles have more energy and move faster, so the frequency of collisions increases — and a greater proportion of collisions have enough energy to react

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Plants are made of different tissues.

Which term describes a group of tissues working together? Tick one box.

  • Organ
  • Organism
  • Organ system
answer: Organ

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 1 is a labelled cross-section through a leaf, showing the upper epidermis, the palisade mesophyll below it, the spongy mesophyll with its air spaces, the lower epidermis with its pores, and a vein carrying xylem and phloem.

Draw one line from each leaf tissue to an important feature of the tissue.

Leaf tissues: Palisade mesophyll, Spongy mesophyll.
Features: contains many air spaces; contains the most chloroplasts; made of dead cells.
answer: Palisade mesophyll → contains the most chloroplasts. Spongy mesophyll → contains many air spaces. (No more than one line may leave a box on the left.)
examiner_note: Figure 1 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Xylem tissue transports water to the leaves.

Which term describes the loss of water from the leaves? Tick one box.

  • Photosynthesis
  • Respiration
  • Transpiration
answer: Transpiration

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which substance strengthens xylem tissue? Tick one box.

  • Glucose
  • Lignin
  • Starch
answer: Lignin

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The upper epidermis is transparent.

Explain why the upper epidermis needs to be transparent. Use Figure 1.
answer: So that light can reach the palisade and spongy mesophyll below it — the layers with the chloroplasts — for photosynthesis
examiner_note: Figure 1 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated at 01.2.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Complete the sentences. Choose answers from the box: chloroplasts   guard cells   meristems   stomata

The pores in the lower epidermis of a leaf are called ............... .
The opening and closing of the pores in the lower epidermis is controlled by ............... .
answer: stomata; guard cells — in that order

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 2 is a photograph of two cells from phloem tissue, labelled cell X and cell Y, with a part A marked inside one of them. Part A contains cell sap.

Name part A in Figure 2.
answer: The (permanent) vacuole
examiner_note: Figure 2 is a third-party photograph. AQA's own paper prints in its place: “Figure 2 cannot be reproduced here due to third-party copyright restrictions”, and names the source as Bentwood and Cronshaw, ‘Cytochemical Localization of Adenosine Triphosphatase in the Phloem of Pisum sativum and its Relation to the Function of Transfer Cells’, Planta Vol. 2, pp. 111–120.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Sugars move from cell Y into cell X against the concentration gradient. Energy is needed to move sugars against the concentration gradient.

Which process moves sugars against the concentration gradient? Tick one box.

  • Active transport
  • Diffusion
  • Osmosis
answer: Active transport

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which cell structures are needed to provide energy to move sugars? Tick one box.

  • Chloroplasts
  • Chromosomes
  • Mitochondria
answer: Mitochondria

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Pathogens cause disease.

How does the skin defend the human body against pathogens?
answer: It is a physical barrier — it stops pathogens entering the body. (Producing antimicrobial secretions, oil, sebum or sweat is also accepted.)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The stomach contains acid to kill pathogens. A scientist investigated the effect of acid on the survival of bacteria. This is the method used.

  1. Prepare four test tubes each with 10 cm3 of culture solution.
  2. Use acid to adjust the pH of the solutions to be pH1, pH2, pH3 and pH5.
  3. Add 1 cm3 of bacteria mixture to each test tube.
  4. Take a 0.1 cm3 sample from each test tube and record the number of live bacteria.
  5. Keep the test tubes at 37 °C for 24 hours.
  6. Repeat step 4.

Table 1 shows some of the results.

Time in hourspH1pH2pH3pH5
0210210210216
2423X63185

What fraction of the bacteria present at 0 hours for pH3 survived for 24 hours? Give your answer in its simplest form.
answer: 3/10 — 63 out of 210, which cancels to 3/10 (0.3 is accepted; 30% is ignored). Getting to 63/210 alone scores 1.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: How many more bacteria were killed at pH1 than at pH5 in 24 hours? Complete the following steps: calculate the number killed at pH1; calculate the number killed at pH5; calculate how many more were killed at pH1 than at pH5.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student calculated value X in Table 1 to be 43.

Suggest how the student calculated this value.
answer: The student took the midpoint between the pH1 and pH3 values, 23 and 63: (63 − 23) ÷ 2 = 20, and 23 + 20 = 43 — or (23 + 63) ÷ 2 = 43 directly. Plotting the data and reading off pH2 is also accepted.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Measles is caused by a virus. The measles vaccine is given to children to prevent them becoming ill with measles.

Draw one line from each blood component to its function when someone is vaccinated against measles.

Blood components: Platelets, White blood cells.
Functions: help clot the blood where the vaccine was injected; produce antibodies to the measles virus; produce the measles skin rash; transport oxygen to the measles virus.
answer: Platelets → help clot the blood where the vaccine was injected. White blood cells → produce antibodies to the measles virus.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 3 is a pair of graphs sharing a year axis from 1940 to about 2015. The top graph is the percentage of children vaccinated: it is zero until 1968, climbs steeply to about 54% by 1972, runs roughly level to about 1977, climbs again to about 92% by 1995, dips to about 80% in the early 2000s and recovers to about 85%. The bottom graph is the number of people with measles in thousands: about 330 in 1940, rising to about 490 by 1950, level at about 490 until 1968, then falling steeply to about 120 by 1978 and on down to almost nothing by 2000.

What year was the measles vaccine first used? Use Figure 3.
answer: 1968 (1969 is accepted)
examiner_note: Figure 3 is a graph in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Describe the trend in the number of people with measles from 1945 to 1975. Use Figure 3.
answer: It increases, then levels off (reaching a maximum between about 1956 and 1968), then decreases. An overall decrease alone scores 1 of the 3.
examiner_note: Figure 3 is a graph in the PDF; what it shows is stated at 03.2.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
In 1998, a scientific paper was published suggesting a link between condition X and one type of measles vaccine.

What happened to the percentage of children vaccinated against measles after the scientific paper was published in 1998? Use Figure 3.
answer: It decreased — from about 92% to about 80% — and then increased again

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Why might the claims made in the scientific paper have affected the percentage of children vaccinated? Tick one box.

  • The measles pathogen did not exist in the UK anymore.
  • Parents were worried their children would get condition X.
  • The health service in the UK did not have any vaccines.
answer: Parents were worried their children would get condition X

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
In 2010, the scientific paper linking condition X and the measles vaccine was shown to be based on false claims.

What should scientists do with scientific research to help detect false claims? Tick one box.

  • Have the research peer reviewed.
  • Publish the research on the internet.
  • Send a research questionnaire to the public.
answer: Have the research peer reviewed

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The person who wrote the scientific paper was paid to research the link between condition X and the measles vaccine.

Why are the claims in the scientific paper likely to be considered not valid?
answer: Any one of: the author was biased; the author was influenced by money; the research was not peer reviewed; there was not enough evidence; the sample size was small. (Simply 'the author was paid' is ignored.)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Starch and sugar are two types of carbohydrate.

Describe the chemical tests that a student could use to show if bread contains starch, and if it contains sugar. You should include the results of a positive test and a negative test for each type of carbohydrate.
answer: Level-marked out of 4, and Level 2 needs both tests. Starch: add iodine solution — it turns blue-black if starch is present, and stays yellow, orange or brown if it is not. Sugar: add Benedict's solution and heat to at least 60 °C — it turns green, yellow, orange or brick red if sugar is present, and stays blue if it is not.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated three types of bread. For each type the student put a square piece of bread into their mouth, did not chew it, and recorded the time taken for the bread to taste sweet. Table 2 shows the results.

Type of breadTime taken for bread to taste sweet in seconds
Brown43
White35
Wholemeal57

Complete the sentences. Choose answers from the box: amylase   fat   lipase   protease   sugar

The starch in the bread was broken down by the enzyme ............... .
The enzyme broke down the starch into ............... .
answer: amylase; sugar — in that order

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What was the independent variable in the investigation? Tick one box.

  • The size of the piece of bread
  • The temperature of the mouth
  • The type of bread
answer: The type of bread

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give two conclusions that can be made from the results in Table 2.
answer: Any two of: white bread tastes sweet in the least time; wholemeal bread takes the most time to taste sweet; brown bread takes more time than white bread to taste sweet. Any correct comparison of two breads scores one mark.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The student improved the investigation. Table 3 shows the results.

Type of breadTest 1Test 2Test 3Mean
Brown38434542
White35313935
Wholemeal585561X

What did the student do to improve the investigation? Use Table 2 and Table 3.
answer: Repeated each type of bread (three times) and calculated a mean

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Calculate value X in Table 3.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Why should the student do the investigation with more people? Tick one box.

  • Each person's sense of taste is different.
  • More people would make the investigation safer.
  • There are many different types of bread.
answer: Each person's sense of taste is different

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Cancer occurs when there is uncontrolled cell division.

Which two factors can cause cancer? Tick two boxes.

  • Antibiotics
  • Ionising radiation
  • Monoclonal antibodies
  • Salmonella
  • Viruses
answer: Ionising radiation and viruses

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What type of cell division occurs in cancerous cells? Tick one box.

  • Binary fission
  • Fertilisation
  • Mitosis
answer: Mitosis

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Complete the sentences. Choose answers from the box: decrease   fertilise   grow   replicate

Before a cell divides, the cell needs to ............... .
Before a cell divides, the DNA in the nucleus needs to ............... .
answer: grow; replicate — in that order

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 4 shows the cell cycle as a pie chart with an arrow running clockwise round the rim. The rim carries ten equally spaced tick marks. The Cell growth stage sector spans four of them, the Copying of chromosomes stage sector spans five, and a small dark sector labelled Stage X spans one.

What percentage of the time taken for the cell cycle does the cell growth stage take? Use Figure 4. Tick one box.

  • 10%
  • 20%
  • 40%
  • 90%
answer: 40% — four of the ten equal divisions
examiner_note: Figure 4 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What happens during stage X of the cell cycle in Figure 4? Tick one box.

  • Chromosomes are pulled to each end of the cell.
  • The cell increases in size and mass.
  • The number of mitochondria increases.
answer: Chromosomes are pulled to each end of the cell — Stage X is mitosis itself, the shortest part of the cycle
examiner_note: Figure 4 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated at 05.4.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 5 is a drawing of an animal cell during cell division, with the chromosomes at each end and a structure Z labelled at the outside edge of the cell.

Name structure Z in Figure 5.
answer: The (cell) membrane
examiner_note: Figure 5 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The image of the cell in Figure 5 is magnified 800 times and has a width of 50 mm.

Calculate the real width of the cell in Figure 5. Give your answer in micrometres (µm). Use the equation:

real width of cell = width of image of cell ÷ magnification
1 mm = 1000 µm

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Some drugs can treat cancer.

Complete the sentences. Choose answers from the box: cells   people   plants   viruses

Preclinical testing of cancer drugs is done using ............... .
To check if the drug is safe, the drug is tested on ............... .
answer: cells; people — in that order

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
In drug trials some patients are given a tablet which does not contain the drug.

What name is given to the tablet that does not contain the drug?
answer: A placebo

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the effect of different concentrations of salt solution on the mass of uncooked pieces of potato. This is the method used.

  1. Cut four pieces of a potato to the same size.
  2. Record the mass of each piece of potato.
  3. Put one of the pieces of potato into a beaker containing 100 cm3 of 0.1 mol/dm3 salt solution.
  4. Repeat step 3 using the other pieces of potato, each in a different concentration of salt solution.
  5. After 20 minutes, remove the pieces of potato from the solutions.
  6. Record the mass of each piece of potato.

Give two control variables the student used in the investigation.
answer: Any two of: the size of the piece of potato; the type of potato (the same potato); the volume of salt solution (100 cm³); the time the pieces are kept in the solution (20 minutes); the potato was uncooked

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The student needed to be sure the measurements were as accurate as possible.

What should be done to each piece of potato after removing from the solution and before measuring the mass?
answer: Blot it — dry the surface

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Name the piece of apparatus the student could use to measure the mass of the pieces of potato.
answer: A balance (weighing scale)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 4 shows the results.

Piece of potatoConcentration of salt solution in mol/dm3Mass at start in gMass after 20 minutes in gChange in gPercentage (%) change in mass
A0.16.26.5+ 0.3+ 4.8
B0.36.86.5− 0.3− 4.4
C0.56.55.8− 0.7− 10.8
D0.76.04.9− 1.1X

What was the resolution of the apparatus used for measuring mass? Use Table 4. Tick one box.

  • 0.01 g
  • 0.1 g
  • 1.0 g
  • 1.1 g
answer: 0.1 g — every mass in the table is given to one decimal place

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Which piece of potato had the greatest change in mass in the investigation? Tick one box: A, B, C or D.
answer: D — it changed by 1.1 g

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Calculate value X in Table 4. Use the equation:

percentage change in mass = (change in mass in grams ÷ mass at start in grams) × 100

Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
answer: −18.3% — 1.1 ÷ 6.0 × 100 = 18.333…, which to one decimal place is 18.3

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the best way to present the data in Table 4? Tick one box.

  • Bar chart
  • Line graph
  • Pie chart
answer: Line graph — concentration is a continuous variable

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Complete the sentences.

Some of the pieces of potato decreased in mass because the potato cells lost ............... .
The decrease in mass was due to a process called ............... .
The structure surrounding each cell in a piece of potato is partially ............... .
answer: water; osmosis; permeable (membrane) — in that order

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Estimate the concentration of salt solution that would not cause a change in mass of these pieces of potato.
answer: Anything from 0.15 to 0.25 mol/dm³ — the percentage change crosses zero between A at 0.1 and B at 0.3

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A person has coronary heart disease.

Which blood vessels are affected by coronary heart disease? Tick one box.

  • Arteries
  • Capillaries
  • Veins
answer: Arteries

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A person's heart stops beating. The person stops breathing. A first-aider pushes down on the person's chest. Pushing down on the person's chest puts pressure on the heart.

Explain why putting pressure on the heart helps the person.
answer: It pushes blood around the body, which gets oxygen to the organs. (Not 'to the lungs'.)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The first-aider also forces air into the person's lungs by blowing into their mouth.

Describe how forcing air into the person's lungs helps the person.
answer: It provides oxygen for respiration

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The person's heart starts to beat again and the person starts breathing. The person has a high level of cholesterol in their blood.

Name one type of drug that would decrease the level of cholesterol in the person's blood.
answer: Statins

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A doctor decides that the person needs to have a stent fitted.

Explain how a stent works to treat coronary heart disease.
answer: The stent opens and keeps open the blocked blood vessel, so more blood — and so more oxygen and glucose — can flow to the heart muscle

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 5 shows the effect of smoking on the risk of developing different cardiovascular diseases.

Cardiovascular diseasePercentage (%) increase in risk compared to people who have never smoked
E14
F20
G29
H70

Give two conclusions that can be made from the data in Table 5.
answer: Any two of: smoking increases the risk of all four diseases; smoking increases the risk of disease H more than any other; smoking increases the risk of disease E less than any other. Two correct comparisons of two diseases also score two.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 6 is a blank graph grid with the bar for cardiovascular disease E already plotted.

Complete Figure 6. You should:

  • label the y-axis
  • add the correct scale to the y-axis
  • plot the data from Table 5
  • label each bar.
answer: Label the y-axis 'Percentage (%) increase in risk compared to people who have never smoked'. The scale is set by the bar already drawn: E is 14%, so one large square is 5%. Plot F at 20, G at 29 and H at 70, and label all four bars. Half a small square of tolerance is allowed; bars touching, and how wide they are, are ignored.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Describe one lifestyle factor that can increase the risk of cardiovascular disease. Do not refer to smoking in your answer.
answer: A poor diet — one high in saturated fat or cholesterol — or a lack of exercise. High alcohol intake and a stressful job are also accepted; 'obesity' and unqualified 'diet' are not.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an inherited disorder caused by a faulty gene.

Where in a cell would the CF gene be found?
answer: In the nucleus (on a chromosome)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
CF affects many organs in the body. The main organs affected are the lungs, the pancreas and the small intestine.

Figure 7 is an outline of the human body with six organs lettered A to F.

Which letters in Figure 7 show the lungs, the pancreas and the small intestine? Tick one box.

  • A, D and E
  • A, E and F
  • B, C and D
  • B, C and F
answer: A, D and E
examiner_note: Figure 7 is artwork in the PDF and is not transcribed; the letters cannot be resolved without it.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The pancreas produces several digestive enzymes. CF reduces the amount of each enzyme that reaches the small intestine.

Explain why a person with CF has difficulty digesting food, and difficulty gaining body mass.
answer: Level-marked out of 6, and Level 3 needs both halves. Digesting food: less lipase, so less fat broken down into fatty acids and glycerol; less amylase, so less starch broken down into glucose; less protease, so less protein broken down into amino acids. Gaining body mass: less absorption of those small soluble molecules, so fewer amino acids for building protein, muscle and tissue, less fat stored, less respiration and so less energy for building new cells and tissues.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Gas exchange happens in the alveoli in the lungs.

Describe three features of the alveoli that help maximise gas exchange.
answer: A large surface area (or surface area to volume ratio); a large capillary network — a good blood supply; walls that are thin, one cell thick. ('Thin alveoli' and 'moist' are ignored.)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
CF reduces the amount of oxygen that can enter the blood from the alveoli.

Explain how a reduced amount of oxygen entering the blood will affect the human body.
answer: There is less aerobic respiration, so less energy is released, which means less muscle contraction — or a reduced metabolism, or an increased breathing rate or heart rate. Alternatively: more anaerobic respiration, so lactic acid is produced, causing muscle fatigue.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The nervous system allows humans to respond to stimuli and coordinate their behaviour.

Complete the order of structures to link a stimulus to a response. Choose answers from the box: coordinator   effector   receptor

stimulus → ............... → ............... → ............... → response
answer: stimulus → receptor → coordinator → effector → response. Either adjacent pair right on its own scores 1.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Some human actions are reflex actions.

What is a reflex action?
answer: Any two of: it is fast or rapid; it is a response or reaction; it is automatic or involuntary — not under conscious control; it protects you from harm

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Which is an example of a reflex action? Tick one box.

  • Blinking in sudden bright light
  • Kicking a ball in a game
  • Writing a message to a friend
answer: Blinking in sudden bright light

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Many reflex actions are movements.

What type of tissue causes movement? Tick one box.

  • Blood
  • Gland
  • Muscle
answer: Muscle

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Many human activities are coordinated by the brain. Figure 1 is a side view of a human brain cut in half, with four structures lettered. A points to the outer layer of the large folded mass filling the top of the skull. B points to a small pea-sized body hanging on a short stalk beneath the middle of the brain. C points to the rounded swelling of the brain stem below that. D points to the cord running down out of the base of the brain. The cerebellum — the smaller ridged mass at the back — is labelled by name.

Which structure in Figure 1 is the pituitary gland? Tick one box: A, B, C or D.
answer: B
examiner_note: Figure 1 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology

subject: Biology

Scientists think that the animals in Figure 2 all evolved from an ancestor that lived about 6 million years ago.

What was the most recent time that the domestic dog and the golden jackal shared a common ancestor? Tick one box.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Scientists think the grey wolf and the domestic dog had a common ancestor. The common ancestor lived about 32 thousand years ago and is now extinct.

Give two possible causes of extinction.
answer: Any two of: drought; an ice age; global warming; volcanic activity; an asteroid collision; new predators or hunters; new disease; competition for food; competition for mates; loss or change of habitat. 'Climate change' alone scores 1.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:

Suggest one reason why wolves began to follow groups of humans.
answer: Any one of: wolves ate the humans; wolves got the left-over food from humans; humans gave food to the wolves

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Some wolves are more aggressive than other wolves.

Describe how selective breeding of wolves could produce a domestic animal that is less aggressive than the wolf.
answer: Breed from the least aggressive wolves, then breed from the least aggressive of their offspring — and keep repeating that over many generations

subject: Biology

Which part of the virus is put into the yeast cell?

  • The viruses may cause an infection.

subject: Biology

Why do people with Type 2 diabetes often have a high concentration of glucose in their blood? Tick one box.

  • The body cells have a high rate of respiration to release energy.
  • The body cells take in a low amount of glucose from the blood.
answer: The body cells take in a low amount of glucose from the blood

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Drug X is used for treating people who have Type 2 diabetes. Scientists investigated the effect of drug X on the concentration of glucose in the blood of mice. This is the method used.

  2. Give each mouse in group A 2 cm3 of water to drink.

Give two control variables used in the investigation.
answer: Any two of: the same diet; the same 8-week duration; the same 30 minutes before the glucose; the same 2 cm³ volume of drink; the same 1 cm³ of glucose solution

subject: Biology

Group B reached a maximum value earlier than group A. Determine how many minutes earlier.
answer: 10 minutes — 30 for group A minus 20 for group B. Anything from 28 to 32 is accepted for group A.
examiner_note: Figure 6 is a graph in the PDF; the two peak times are the mark scheme's own readings.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024

Gardeners can grow plants from seeds and from cuttings taken from adult plants. A gardener investigated the growth of roots on cuttings from a geranium plant. This is the method used.

Tube 1 contains no chemical Q. Tube 1 is a control.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The gardener has four types of geranium plant: A, B, C and D. Plant A produces larger, more brightly-coloured flowers than any of the other plants. The gardener wants to grow more plants of type A.

Explain why the gardener chooses to take cuttings from plant A instead of growing seeds from plant A.
answer: Level-marked out of 4. Cuttings are quicker — no waiting for flowers, fruit and seed. They are asexual reproduction, so there is no fusing of gametes and no mixing of alleles from two parents: it is mitosis, which copies the genetic material exactly, rather than meiosis. So every offspring is a clone of plant A and has the same large, brightly-coloured flowers, where seeds would vary through pollination from other geraniums. That also means consistent quality and a quicker turnover for the gardener.

subject: Biology

html:
In 1866, a monk called Gregor Mendel published the results of his investigations into inheritance in pea plants. Pea seeds can be round or wrinkled in shape. Mendel crossed pea plants that produced round seeds with pea plants that produced wrinkled seeds. Figure 10 shows the result: plant 1 (round seeds) crossed with plant 2 (wrinkled seeds) gave plants 3 and 4, which all produced round seeds.

Use these symbols for the alleles: R = dominant allele for round seeds, r = recessive allele for wrinkled seeds.

In Figure 10, the genotype of plant 1 is RR. Give the genotype of plant 2.
answer: rr — homozygous recessive
examiner_note: Figures 9 and 10 are artwork in the PDF; what Figure 10 shows is stated in the question.

Female

answer: 3 : 1 — three of the four genotypes carry at least one R

subject: Biology

Some of the offspring in Figure 11 are homozygous and some are heterozygous.

What does 'heterozygous' mean?
answer: Having two different alleles of a gene. (Not 'two different genes'.)

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Mendel published his work in 1866.

Suggest two reasons why the importance of Mendel's work was not recognised until the early 1900s.
answer: Any two of: other scientists were not aware of his work, or it was published in an obscure journal and lost for years; other theories such as blending inheritance were accepted at the time; he was not considered a scientist — he was only a monk; his mathematical approach was a novel idea nobody understood; peas gave unusual results compared with other species, and his results were not corroborated; later discoveries were what made his work relevant.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Evolution of new species occurs by mutation and natural selection.

What is a mutation?
answer: A change in the DNA — in a base, in the base sequence, in a gene or allele, or in part of or the number of chromosomes

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html: Describe the process of natural selection.
answer: Any three of: there is variation between members of a species; the better adapted individuals survive; those survivors reproduce; and they pass on the favourable alleles to their offspring

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Which scientists suggested the theory of evolution by natural selection? Tick one box.

  • Alexander Fleming and Carl Woese
  • Alfred Wallace and Alexander Fleming
  • Alfred Wallace and Charles Darwin
  • Charles Darwin and Carl Woese
answer: Alfred Wallace and Charles Darwin

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The hoverfly and the wasp are insects with bright yellow and black markings. Figure 12 is a pair of photographs of a hoverfly and a wasp, side by side, showing how similar their yellow and black banding is. The wasp has a sting to defend itself against predators. The hoverfly does not have a sting. Hoverflies and wasps live in the same habitat.

Explain how having yellow and black markings helps the hoverfly survive.
answer: The hoverfly looks like a wasp — the pattern of markings is similar. Predators avoid wasps so that they do not get stung. So a predator does not attack or eat the hoverfly either.
examiner_note: Figure 12 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Peat bogs are estimated to contain twice as much carbon as all the world's forests. Figure 13 is a cut-away section through part of a peat bog: a living surface of moss and sundew plants, a layer A just below it, and a darker layer B beneath that. Layer A contains a lot of air. Layer B contains the dead remains of plants, has a low pH, contains very little oxygen, and contains carbon dioxide and methane.

Explain why most of the dead remains of plants in layer B do not decay.
answer: There is not enough oxygen for aerobic respiration, so less energy is released, in the decomposers — the microorganisms, bacteria and fungi. Alternatively: the low pH denatures their enzymes, so there are fewer reactions and less energy released in the decomposers.
examiner_note: Figure 13 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
The peat bog in Figure 13 is a stable community. The moss produces biomass at a rate of 340 g/m2/year.

What is the approximate biomass of the moss that becomes biomass in primary consumers? Tick one box.

  • 0.34 g/m2/year
  • 3.4 g/m2/year
  • 34 g/m2/year
  • 340 g/m2/year
answer: 34 g/m²/year — about 10% of the biomass passes to the next trophic level

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024

What substance can the sundew plant make using the phosphates? Tick one box.

  • Cellulose
  • DNA

  • Starch

subject: Biology
name: Paper 2 — June 2024
html:
Humans have destroyed large areas of peat bog to collect peat. The peat provides fuel and provides compost for gardeners to use. The peat comes from layer B. Figure 14 is a photograph of peat being cut and removed from a bog.

Explain how the destruction of peat bogs and the use of peat affects the temperature of the Earth's atmosphere.
answer: The temperature increases — global warming. Carbon dioxide is released from the peat bog; carbon dioxide is produced by burning the peat and by its decay once it is exposed; and methane is released from the bog as well. There are also fewer plants left to take carbon dioxide in by photosynthesis.
