In Step 2 the acid is added to the alkali until the solution is neutralised. The volume of acid added is then read from equipment C.

Name a suitable indicator for use in Step 2 of the titration.
answer: Methyl orange or phenolphthalein (litmus is accepted). Universal indicator is not.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give one observation that shows the alkali is neutralised.
answer: A colour change

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give two ways to make sure that the volume of acid added is accurate.
answer: Any two of: swirl the flask; add the acid drop by drop near the end point; read the burette at eye level, at the bottom of the meniscus; make sure there are no bubbles in the burette; stand the flask on a white tile; repeat and take a mean

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 5 shows the reading on equipment C at the end of Step 2: a close-up of the burette scale, marked in 0.1 cm3 divisions with 16 and 17 labelled, and the bottom of the meniscus sitting six small divisions below the 16 mark.

What is the reading on equipment C? Tick one box.

  • 16.4 cm3
  • 16.6 cm3
  • 17.4 cm3
  • 17.6 cm3
answer: 16.6 cm³ — a burette is numbered downwards from the top, and the meniscus is read at its bottom
examiner_note: Figure 5 is artwork in the PDF; the reading it shows is the mark scheme's own.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student did a different titration. Table 1 shows the results.

Trial 1Trial 2Trial 3
Volume of acid added in cm325.323.723.6

Which two results should be used to calculate the mean volume of acid added? Tick one box.

  • Trial 1 and Trial 2
  • Trial 1 and Trial 3
  • Trial 2 and Trial 3
answer: Trial 2 and Trial 3 — they are concordant, within 0.1 cm³ of each other; trial 1 is the rough titration

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A salt is produced when an acid neutralises an alkali. Barium chloride is a salt containing the ions Ba2+ and Cl−.

What is the formula of barium chloride? Tick one box.

  • BaCl
  • BaCl2
  • Ba2Cl
  • Ba2Cl2
answer: BaCl₂ — two 1− ions balance one 2+ ion

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about energy changes of reactions. Zinc reacts with copper sulfate solution:

zinc + copper sulfate → zinc sulfate + copper

What type of reaction is this? Tick one box.

  • Combustion
  • Decomposition
  • Displacement
answer: Displacement

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Calculate the percentage (%) by mass of copper in copper sulfate (CuSO4). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

Relative atomic mass (Ar): Cu = 63.5
Relative formula mass (Mr): CuSO4 = 159.5
answer: 39.8% — 63.5 ÷ 159.5 × 100 = 39.81191…, which to 3 significant figures is 39.8

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated the energy change in the reaction between zinc and copper sulfate solution. This is the method used.

  1. Measure 25 cm3 of copper sulfate solution into a polystyrene cup.
  2. Weigh 0.20 g of zinc powder.
  3. Add the zinc powder to the copper sulfate solution.
  4. Measure the highest temperature reached by the mixture.
  5. Repeat steps 1 to 4 using different masses of zinc powder.

Control variables are used to make an investigation a fair test.

Which is a control variable in the investigation? Tick one box.

  • Highest temperature reached by the mixture
  • Mass of zinc powder
  • Volume of copper sulfate solution
answer: Volume of copper sulfate solution

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 6 plots the highest temperature reached against the mass of zinc powder added. The points climb steeply from 22 °C with no zinc to 47 °C at 0.80 g, and from there they stay level at about 47 °C for every larger mass.

What is the minimum mass of zinc powder needed to react with all the copper sulfate solution? Use Figure 6.
answer: 0.80 g — the mass at which the temperature stops rising, so all the copper sulfate has reacted
examiner_note: Figure 6 is a graph in the PDF; the two values quoted are the mark scheme's own readings.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: What is the maximum temperature change in the reaction between zinc powder and 25 cm3 of copper sulfate solution? Use Figure 6.
answer: 25 °C — 47 °C minus the starting 22 °C

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
25 cm3 of copper sulfate solution contained 6.75 g of copper sulfate.

Calculate the concentration of the solution in g/dm3. You should calculate the volume of the solution in dm3 (1000 cm3 = 1 dm3) and use:

concentration in g/dm3 = mass of copper sulfate in grams ÷ volume of solution in dm3

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Another student investigated the energy change of the reaction between sodium hydrogencarbonate and hydrochloric acid, measuring the lowest temperature reached for different masses of sodium hydrogencarbonate. Figure 7 plots those results: the first five points fall steadily as more is added, and the last four sit level at the bottom.

Draw two straight lines of best fit on Figure 7. The lines should cross.
answer: One line of best fit through the first five points — the falling part — and a second through the last four, the level part. Maximum 1 mark if the lines do not intersect.
examiner_note: Figure 7 is a graph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which statement describes the energy change in the reaction shown in Figure 7? Tick one box.

  • Energy is transferred to the surroundings so the reaction is endothermic.
  • Energy is transferred to the surroundings so the reaction is exothermic.
  • Energy is taken in from the surroundings so the reaction is endothermic.
  • Energy is taken in from the surroundings so the reaction is exothermic.
answer: Energy is taken in from the surroundings so the reaction is endothermic — the temperature falls

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about small particles.

What is the approximate number of atoms in a nanoparticle? Tick one box.

  • A few hundred atoms
  • A few thousand atoms
  • A few million atoms
  • A few billion atoms
answer: A few hundred atoms

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Nanoparticles of some elements can be used as catalysts.

Which element is most likely to be used as a catalyst? Use the periodic table. Tick one box.

  • Aluminium
  • Iron
  • Magnesium
answer: Iron — it is the only transition metal of the three

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Nanoparticles are used in sun creams and in wound dressings. A wound dressing is placed next to the skin to prevent infection; Figure 8 is a photograph of one. Table 2 shows some information about substances used in the form of nanoparticles.

SubstanceProperty
CarbonStrong
Silicon dioxideHard
SilverKills bacteria
Titanium dioxideBlocks light

Draw one line from each use to the best substance for that use.

Uses: Sun creams, Wound dressings.
Substances: carbon; silicon dioxide; silver; titanium dioxide.
answer: Sun creams → titanium dioxide, because it blocks light. Wound dressings → silver, because it kills bacteria.
examiner_note: Figure 8 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 9 shows a cubic nanoparticle with each edge labelled 4 nm.

Calculate the surface area of the cubic nanoparticle, its volume, and the simplest whole number ratio of surface area : volume. Use the equation:

surface area of cubic nanoparticle = 6 × surface area of one face
answer: Surface area = 6 × 4² = 96 nm². Volume = 4³ = 64 nm³. Ratio 96 : 64, which simplifies to 3 : 2.
examiner_note: Figure 9 is artwork in the PDF; the edge length it is labelled with is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about carbon and carbon compounds. An atom of carbon is represented as 136C.

What is the number of protons in this atom of carbon? Tick one box.

  • 1
  • 6
  • 7
  • 13
answer: 6 — the bottom number is the atomic number

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the number of neutrons in this atom of carbon? Tick one box.

  • 1
  • 6
  • 7
  • 13
answer: 7 — the mass number 13 minus the 6 protons

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the number of electrons in this atom of carbon? Tick one box.

  • 1
  • 6
  • 7
  • 13
answer: 6 — an atom is neutral, so it has as many electrons as protons

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 10 shows the structure of a carbon compound as a displayed formula: two carbon atoms joined to each other, with three fluorine atoms bonded to each.

Complete the formula of the carbon compound: C__F__
answer: C₂F₆
examiner_note: Figure 10 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Methane is a carbon compound, exists as small molecules, and has a low boiling point.

What is the reason for the low boiling point of methane? Tick one box.

  • Covalent bonds and intermolecular forces are weak.
  • Only covalent bonds are weak.
  • Only intermolecular forces are weak.
answer: Only intermolecular forces are weak — the covalent bonds inside the molecule are strong and are not broken when it boils

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Buckminsterfullerene (C60) is a form of carbon and was the first fullerene to be discovered.

What is the shape of a buckminsterfullerene molecule? Tick one box.

  • Cubic
  • Cylindrical
  • Spherical
answer: Spherical

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Graphite is a form of carbon. Figure 11 represents its structure: flat sheets of carbon atoms joined in hexagons, with the sheets stacked above one another.

How many covalent bonds does each carbon atom form in graphite? Tick one box.

  • 1
  • 2
  • 3
  • 4
examiner_note: Figure 11 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Diamond is another form of carbon. Figure 12 represents its structure: carbon atoms joined in a three-dimensional network, each one bonded to the atoms around it.

Describe the structure and bonding in diamond.
answer: It is a giant structure (a lattice) of atoms joined by covalent bonds, and each carbon atom forms four of them
examiner_note: Figure 12 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about electrolysis and the extraction of metals.

Why can some molten substances be electrolysed? Tick one box.

  • Electrons can move through the molten substance to the electrodes.
  • Ions can move through the molten substance to the electrodes.
  • Protons can move through the molten substance to the electrodes.
answer: Ions can move through the molten substance to the electrodes

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 3 shows the products of the electrolysis of some molten compounds. Complete Table 3.

Molten compoundProduct at negative electrodeProduct at positive electrode
Lead chloride Chlorine
Potassium iodidePotassium 
 ZincBromine
answer: Lead chloride gives lead at the negative electrode. Potassium iodide gives iodine at the positive electrode. The third compound is zinc bromide.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Aluminium is extracted by electrolysing molten aluminium oxide.

Balance the equation for the reaction. Choose numbers from the box: 2   3   4   5

2 Al2O3 → ___ Al + ___ O2
answer: 2 Al₂O₃ → 4 Al + 3 O₂. Either number alone scores 1.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of aluminium oxide (Al2O3).

Relative atomic masses (Ar): O = 16, Al = 27

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 13 shows part of the reactivity series with the non-metal carbon included, most reactive first: potassium, lithium, carbon, zinc, tin, gold.

Metals can be extracted from their compounds by electrolysis and by reduction with carbon. Electrolysis is more expensive than reduction with carbon.

Predict one metal that would be extracted by each method. Use Figure 13.
answer: By electrolysis: potassium or lithium — a metal above carbon, which carbon cannot displace. By carbon reduction: zinc or tin — a metal below carbon.
examiner_note: Figure 13 is artwork in the PDF; the series it shows is written out in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about chemical cells.

A student connects four 1.5 V cells in series to make a battery. What is the total voltage produced by the battery?

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A chemical cell can be made using two different metals in contact with an electrolyte. Figure 14 shows one: two metal strips, labelled metal A and metal B, standing in a beaker of solution and connected to a voltmeter.

Which is a suitable electrolyte for a chemical cell? Tick one box.

  • Pure water
  • Solid lead bromide
  • Sodium chloride solution
answer: Sodium chloride solution — it contains ions that are free to move
examiner_note: Figure 14 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student made the hypothesis: 'The voltage produced by a cell depends on the difference in the reactivity of metal A and metal B.'

Plan an investigation to test this hypothesis. Your plan should produce valid results. Use Figure 14.
answer: Level-marked out of 6. Set up the cell as in Figure 14: pour the electrolyte into a beaker, stand two different metals in it, connect them to a voltmeter and measure the voltage. Repeat with different pairs of metals, keeping one metal the same each time so the comparison is about the other. Use the same type, volume and concentration of electrolyte every time.
examiner_note: Figure 14 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated at 07.2.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student produced a salt by reacting copper carbonate with sulfuric acid. This is the method used.

  1. Measure 50 cm3 of sulfuric acid into a beaker.
  2. Add copper carbonate powder.
  3. Stir the mixture.
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 until copper carbonate is in excess.
  5. Filter the mixture.
  6. Warm the filtrate gently until crystals start to appear.
  7. Leave the solution to cool and crystallise.

Complete the word equation for the reaction.

copper carbonate + sulfuric acid → ............... + ............... + carbon dioxide
answer: copper sulfate + water (CuSO₄ and H₂O are accepted)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give one observation the student could make during Step 4 which shows that the copper carbonate is in excess.
answer: Solid remains in the mixture — or there is no more effervescence, bubbling or fizzing

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Give one reason for filtering the mixture in Step 5.
answer: To remove the excess copper carbonate

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Name the equipment that can be used to warm the filtrate gently in Step 6.
answer: An electric heater, or a water bath. (A Bunsen burner is ignored.)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The maximum theoretical mass of the salt that could be produced using 50 cm3 of the sulfuric acid is 12.5 g. The percentage yield of the salt is 92.8%.

Calculate the mass of salt actually produced. Use the equation:

% yield = (mass of salt actually produced ÷ maximum theoretical mass of salt that could be produced) × 100

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Some salts can be produced by reacting sulfuric acid with a metal. Neither copper nor sodium is used to produce a salt with sulfuric acid.

Give one reason why each metal is not used.
answer: Copper: it does not react with the acid — it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it will not displace hydrogen. Sodium: the reaction is dangerous — it could explode, or get too hot.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
This question is about the periodic table. Sodium and potassium are in Group 1.

Give one similarity and one difference between the electronic structures of sodium and potassium.
answer: Similarity: both have one electron in their outer shell. Difference: sodium has 3 shells and potassium has 4.

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Group 1 elements react with water.

Give two observations made when potassium reacts with water.
answer: Any two of: effervescence, bubbling or fizzing; the potassium floats; it moves around; it gets smaller; it melts or forms a ball; a flame; an explosion

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Potassium hydroxide solution is produced when potassium reacts with water.

What is the colour of universal indicator when added to potassium hydroxide solution? Give one reason for your answer.
answer: Blue, violet or purple — because the solution is alkaline (it contains hydroxide, OH⁻, ions)

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The elements in Group 7 are called the halogens. A more reactive halogen can displace a less reactive halogen from a solution of its salt.

Which combination of solutions will produce a reaction when mixed? Tick one box.

  • Chlorine and potassium fluoride
  • Chlorine and potassium bromide
  • Bromine and potassium fluoride
  • Bromine and potassium chloride
answer: Chlorine and potassium bromide

subject: Chemistry
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which of the following describes the trends going down Group 7? Tick one box.

  • Relative molecular mass decreases and boiling point decreases.
  • Relative molecular mass decreases and boiling point increases.

html: Which of the following diagrams shows the electric field pattern around the negatively charged metal dome? The options are a sphere with straight field lines drawn radially, differing in which way the arrowheads point and whether the lines are radial at all. Tick one box.
answer: The one with straight radial lines pointing INWARDS, towards the dome — a field line points the way a positive charge would be pushed, and a negative charge attracts one
examiner_note: The field-pattern options are artwork in the PDF and the answer is a drawing in the scheme; both are described rather than reproduced.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 3 shows the negatively charged metal dome and an earthed conductor a short distance away from it, with air in the gap.

The air between the dome and the earthed conductor is an insulator.

Complete the sentence. Choose the answer from the box: efficiency   resistance   temperature

The air between the dome and the earthed conductor has a high ............... .
answer: resistance
examiner_note: Figure 3 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The earthed conductor is moved closer to the metal dome. A spark jumps from the dome to the earthed conductor.

Complete the sentence. Choose the answer from the box: earthed   ionised   neutral

The spark jumps because the air around the charged dome has become ............... .
answer: ionised

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which particles are transferred when the spark jumps from the negatively charged metal dome to the earthed conductor? Tick one box.

  • Electrons
  • Neutrons
  • Protons
answer: Electrons

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The potential difference between the metal dome and earth is 300 000 V. When the spark jumps there is a charge flow of 0.000 002 C.

Calculate the energy transferred by the spark. Use the equation:

energy transferred = charge flow × potential difference

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 4 is a photograph of a student putting a coin into a vending machine that sells food. The vending machine is connected to the mains electricity supply.

What is the frequency of the mains electricity supply in the UK? Tick one box.

  • 50 hertz
  • 60 hertz
  • 100 hertz
answer: 50 hertz
examiner_note: Figure 4 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the potential difference of the mains electricity supply in the UK? Tick one box.

  • 12 volts
  • 230 volts
  • 20 000 volts
answer: 230 volts

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The vending machine identifies the value of the coin by measuring the resistance of the coin. The machine applies a potential difference of 0.45 V across the coin. The current in the coin is 0.75 A.

Calculate the resistance of the coin. Use the equation:

resistance = potential difference ÷ current

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The temperature inside the vending machine is monitored using an electrical circuit. Figure 5 shows part of it: a battery with a thermistor and a 200 Ω resistor in series.

The circuit symbol for the thermistor in Figure 5 is wrong.

What is the circuit symbol for a thermistor? The options are variations on a rectangle with a line through it. Tick one box.
answer: A rectangle with a line entering at the bottom left, running up and then turning to the right along the top — the resistor box with the diagonal-and-foot marking that means temperature-dependent
examiner_note: Figure 5 and the symbol options are artwork in the PDF and the answer is a drawing in the scheme; both are described rather than reproduced.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
How could the potential difference (pd) across the resistor be calculated? Tick one box.

  • pd across battery − pd across thermistor
  • pd across battery + pd across thermistor
  • pd across battery × pd across thermistor
  • pd across battery ÷ pd across thermistor
answer: pd across battery − pd across thermistor — in a series circuit the two pds add up to the supply pd

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The battery in Figure 5 supplies 3.0 V and the fixed resistor is 200 Ω.

At one temperature, the thermistor in Figure 5 has a resistance of 200 Ω.

What is the potential difference across the thermistor at this temperature? Give a reason for your answer. Tick one box.

  • 0.0 V
  • 1.0 V
  • 1.5 V
  • 2.0 V
answer: 1.5 V, because the thermistor has the same resistance as the resistor — so the potential difference is shared equally between them, and each gets half of the 3.0 V

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 6 is a graph of the resistance of the thermistor against temperature: the resistance falls steeply as the temperature rises, passing 600 Ω at 10 °C and 200 Ω at 15 °C.

When the temperature of the thermistor is 10 °C, the resistance of the thermistor is 600 Ω.

Calculate the change in resistance when the temperature increased from 10 °C to 15 °C.
answer: 400 Ω — the resistance at 15 °C is 200 Ω, and 600 − 200 = 400
examiner_note: Figure 6 is a graph in the PDF; the value at 15 °C is the mark scheme's own reading.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
In a ride at a theme park, a person is strapped into a pod that is attached to two stretched bungee cords. The bungee cords behave like springs. Figure 7 is a photograph of a person using the ride, held down at ground level with the two cords running up to towers on either side.

How is the extension of each bungee cord calculated? Tick one box.

  • stretched length + original length
  • stretched length − original length
  • stretched length × original length
  • stretched length ÷ original length
answer: stretched length − original length
examiner_note: Figure 7 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Before the pod is released, the extension of each bungee cord is 7.5 m.

spring constant of the bungee cord = 800 N/m

Calculate the elastic potential energy stored in each stretched bungee cord. Use the equation:

elastic potential energy = 0.5 × spring constant × (extension)2

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The maximum speed of the pod is 15 m/s. The mass of the pod is 240 kg.

Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the pod. Use the equation:

kinetic energy = 0.5 × mass × (speed)2

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Which equation links gravitational field strength (g), gravitational potential energy (Ep), height (h) and mass (m)? Tick one box.

  • Ep = m × g ÷ h
  • Ep = m ÷ (g × h)
  • Ep = m × g × h
answer: E_p = m × g × h

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The pod has 24 000 J of gravitational potential energy when at its maximum height. The mass of the pod is 240 kg.

gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg

Calculate the maximum height reached by the pod.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Why is the maximum gravitational potential energy of the pod less than the initial elastic potential energy of the bungee cords? Tick two boxes.

  • Energy is created.
  • Energy is destroyed.
  • Energy is transferred to the surroundings.
  • Work is done against air resistance.
  • Work is done by the force of gravity.
  • Work is done by the person in the pod.
answer: Energy is transferred to the surroundings; work is done against air resistance

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 8 shows a measuring cylinder containing some water. It is graduated from 0.0 at the bottom to 10.0 at the top, with a line every 0.2 cm3.

What range of volumes can be measured using the measuring cylinder? Tick one box.

  • 0.0 to 0.2 cm3
  • 0.0 to 2.0 cm3
  • 0.0 to 10.0 cm3
answer: 0.0 to 10.0 cm³ — the range is the whole scale; 0.2 cm³ is the resolution
examiner_note: Figure 8 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student used the measuring cylinder to measure the volume of a metal ring. The student tied the metal ring to some very thin string and lowered the ring into the measuring cylinder. The student could have used thick string instead of thin string.

How would using thick string have affected the measured volume of the metal ring? Tick one box.

  • The measured volume would be smaller.
  • The measured volume would not be affected.
  • The measured volume would be larger.
answer: The measured volume would be larger — the string itself displaces water too

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 1 shows the results.

Volume of water in cm3Volume of water and ring in cm3Volume of ring in cm3
5.05.4X

Calculate value X in Table 1.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The student measured the volume of the ring three times. The results were all the same.

Which of the following describes the student's results? Tick one box.

  • The results are anomalies.
  • The results are repeatable.
  • The results contain random errors.
answer: The results are repeatable

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The student used a balance to measure the mass of the ring. Figure 9 is a photograph of the balance. The student noticed that the balance had a reading of 0.02 g when there was no object on it.

How should the student correct this error after the mass of the ring had been measured? Tick one box.

  • Add 0.02 to the measurement
  • Divide the measurement by 0.02
  • Multiply the measurement by 0.02
  • Subtract 0.02 from the measurement
answer: Subtract 0.02 from the measurement — it is a zero error and every reading is 0.02 g too big
examiner_note: Figure 9 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Write down the equation which links density (ρ), mass (m) and volume (V).
answer: density = mass ÷ volume, or ρ = m ÷ V

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A different metal ring has a volume of 0.3 cm3. The density of this ring is 22 g/cm3.

Calculate the mass of this ring. Give your answer in grams.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated how the pressure in a fixed mass of air varies with the volume of the air. Figure 10 shows the equipment used: a sealed syringe with its nozzle connected to a pressure gauge. When the plunger was pushed slowly into the syringe, the temperature of the air stayed the same.

How did pushing the plunger in affect the volume of air in the syringe? Tick one box.

  • The volume decreased.
  • The volume stayed the same.
  • The volume increased.
answer: The volume decreased
examiner_note: Figure 10 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
How did pushing the plunger in affect the distance between the air particles in the syringe? Tick one box.

  • The distance decreased.
  • The distance stayed the same.
  • The distance increased.
answer: The distance decreased

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
How did pushing the plunger in affect the frequency of collisions between the air particles and the syringe walls? Tick one box.

  • The frequency of collisions decreased.
  • The frequency of collisions stayed the same.
  • The frequency of collisions increased.
answer: The frequency of collisions increased

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
How did pushing the plunger in affect the air pressure in the syringe? Tick one box.

  • The air pressure decreased.
  • The air pressure stayed the same.
  • The air pressure increased.
answer: The air pressure increased

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A fire piston is a special type of syringe that can be used to start fires. Figure 11 shows one: a narrow cylinder with a plunger, and a small piece of cotton wool in the bottom. The plunger is pushed quickly downwards and compresses the air. When the air is compressed quickly, the temperature of the air increases.

How does an increase in temperature affect the mean speed of the air particles inside the syringe? Tick one box.

  • The mean speed of the particles decreases.
  • The mean speed of the particles does not change.
  • The mean speed of the particles increases.
answer: The mean speed of the particles increases
examiner_note: Figure 11 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
When the air is hot enough, a small piece of cotton wool in the piston catches fire. The energy transferred to the air in the piston is 0.0130 J. The mass of air in the piston is 2.60 × 10−8 kg.

specific heat capacity of air = 1010 J/kg °C

Calculate the temperature change of the air. Use the Physics Equations Sheet.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A teacher measured the background radiation in a laboratory.

Which sources of background radiation are natural and which are man-made? Tick one box in each row: cosmic rays, medical X-rays, nuclear accidents, radon gas.
answer: Natural: cosmic rays and radon gas. Man-made: medical X-rays and nuclear accidents. Two or three right scores 1 of the 2.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The teacher measured the radiation emitted by four different types of radioactive rock. Figure 12 shows the equipment: a detector clamped above a bench, with a rock placed below it and a space for a sheet of material in between. Each rock was placed below the detector one at a time and the radiation recorded as counts in 1 minute, with different materials between rock and detector.

Table 2 shows the results.

Number of counts in 1 minuteNo materialOne sheet of paperThick aluminium sheet
No rock212022
Rock A45044818
Rock B385387356
Rock C8702120
Rock D620473214

Which radioactive rock emitted only alpha radiation? Give a reason for your answer. Tick one box: Rock A, Rock B, Rock C or Rock D.
answer: Rock C — one sheet of paper dropped its count from 870 to 21, the background level, because alpha is stopped by paper and is the least penetrating
examiner_note: Figure 12 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Which radioactive rock emitted only beta radiation? Give a reason for your answer. Tick one box: Rock A, Rock B, Rock C or Rock D.
answer: Rock A — paper made almost no difference (450 to 448) but thick aluminium dropped it to 18, the background level, because beta is stopped by aluminium and not by paper

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The teacher took safety precautions during the experiment.

Which precaution would prevent the teacher from becoming contaminated by the radioactive rocks? Tick one box.

  • Displaying the radiation hazard symbol
  • Handling the rocks with clean hands
  • Wearing protective gloves
answer: Wearing protective gloves — contamination is getting the radioactive material itself on you

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the activity of each rock after one half-life? Tick one box.

  • The activity is a quarter of the original activity.
  • The activity is half the original activity.
  • The activity is double the original activity.
  • The activity is zero.
answer: The activity is half the original activity

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
How does the activity of a radioactive source affect the risk of harm from the source? Tick one box.

  • The smaller the activity, the greater the risk of harm.
  • The activity does not affect the risk of harm.
  • The greater the activity, the greater the risk of harm.
answer: The greater the activity, the greater the risk of harm

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
An electrical appliance is connected to the mains electricity supply using a three-core cable. Figure 13 shows one, cut back to reveal three insulated wires inside an outer sheath.

What colour is the insulation covering the live wire inside the cable? Tick one box.

  • Blue
  • Brown
  • Green and yellow
  • Orange
answer: Brown
examiner_note: Figure 13 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What colour is the insulation covering the neutral wire inside the cable? Tick one box.

  • Blue
  • Brown
  • Green and yellow
  • Orange
answer: Blue

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The plug connected to the cable contains a fuse. A fuse contains a wire that is designed to melt when the current is too great.

What is the circuit symbol for a fuse? The options are variations on a rectangle with a line through or beside it. Tick one box.
answer: A rectangle with a horizontal line drawn through it, the line continuing out of both ends
examiner_note: The symbol options are artwork in the PDF and the answer is a drawing in the scheme; both are described rather than reproduced.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The wire in the fuse melts when there is a charge flow of 2.0 C in a time of 0.40 s.

Calculate the current in the wire when it melts. Use the equation:

current = charge flow ÷ time

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The mass of the wire is 0.016 g.

specific latent heat of fusion of the wire = 60 000 J/kg

Calculate the change in thermal energy needed to melt the wire. Use the Physics Equations Sheet.
answer: 0.96 J — convert 0.016 g to 1.6 × 10⁻⁵ kg first, then E = 0.000016 × 60 000

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The fuse transfers some energy to the surroundings as it melts.

How does transferring energy to the surroundings affect the total energy needed to melt the fuse? Tick one box.

  • The total energy will be smaller.
  • The total energy will be the same.
  • The total energy will be greater.
answer: The total energy will be greater

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student had an unknown electrical component inside a sealed box. Figure 14 shows the circuit used to identify it: a cell, a variable resistor, an ammeter in series with the sealed box, and a voltmeter across it. The student varied the potential difference across the component and measured the current.

Table 3 shows the results when the potential difference was 6.0 V.

Potential difference in volts1st reading2nd reading3rd readingMean
6.00.260.210.25X

Calculate value X in Table 3.
answer: 0.24 A — (0.26 + 0.21 + 0.25) ÷ 3. Treating 0.21 as an anomaly and taking (0.26 + 0.25) ÷ 2 = 0.255 also scores both marks.
examiner_note: Figure 14 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 15 shows the results as a graph of current against potential difference. The line passes through the origin, rises steeply at first and then bends over so that it gets less steep as the potential difference increases; at 3.0 V the current is 0.17 A.

Calculate the power of the component when the potential difference across the component is 3.0 V. Use Figure 15 and the equation:

power = potential difference × current
answer: 0.51 W — read 0.17 A off the graph at 3.0 V, then 3.0 × 0.17. Any current from 0.16 to 0.18 A is accepted.
examiner_note: Figure 15 is a graph in the PDF; the current at 3.0 V is the mark scheme's own reading.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Complete the sentence. Choose the answer from the box: decreases   stays the same   increases

As the potential difference across the component increases, the gradient of the graph ............... .
answer: decreases

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
What is the component in the sealed box? Tick one box.

  • Diode
  • Filament lamp
  • Resistor at constant temperature
answer: Filament lamp — the curve bends over because the filament heats up and its resistance rises

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Figure 16 is a photograph of a wind turbine. Wind turbines may generate electricity when the electricity is not needed. Two methods that can be used to store the energy from the turbine are:

Method A: Heating water to a high temperature.
Method B: Pumping water uphill into a reservoir.

Which energy store increases when water is heated?
answer: The thermal (internal) energy store — or the kinetic store of the water particles
examiner_note: Figure 16 is a photograph in the PDF and is not transcribed.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Which energy store increases when water is pumped uphill into a reservoir?
answer: The gravitational potential energy store

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Table 4 shows information about the two methods of storing energy.

MethodEnergy stored per 100 kg of water in kJPercentage of stored energy wastedInstallation
A: Increasing water temperature by 80 °C33 60040%Anywhere
B: Pumping water uphill to a height of 500 m49025%High mountains

Compare the advantages and disadvantages of the two methods of storing energy. Include calculations in your answer.
answer: Level-marked out of 4, and Level 2 needs a calculation that compares the two. Method A: useful energy per 100 kg = 20 160 kJ, wasted = 13 440 kJ, efficiency 60%; it stores far more energy per 100 kg and can be installed anywhere, but the hot water needs insulating. Method B: useful = 367.5 kJ, wasted = 122.5 kJ, efficiency 75%; more efficient, but it needs a high mountain site.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Decreasing the amount of carbon dioxide released by different activities will help slow down climate change. Transport and generating electricity are the two activities that released the largest amounts of carbon dioxide in the UK in 2018.

Explain one change that would reduce the amount of carbon dioxide released by each activity.
answer: Transport: stop burning petrol or diesel, and use electric or hydrogen cars, a bicycle, public transport or walking instead. Generating electricity: stop using coal, oil or gas, and use renewables or nuclear instead — or use fewer appliances, to cut the demand for electricity generated from fossil fuels. Two marks for each activity.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The process of nuclear fission is used in nuclear power stations. Figure 17 shows the process: a neutron striking a uranium nucleus, which splits into two smaller nuclei and releases three more neutrons and a burst of radiation.

Complete the sentences. Choose answers from the box: electrons   gamma rays   neutrons   nuclei   protons

In nuclear power stations, energy is released from uranium ............... .
The uranium in Figure 17 splits into two parts and releases three ............... .
The process of nuclear fission releases electromagnetic radiation in the form of ............... .
answer: nuclei; neutrons; gamma rays — this order only
examiner_note: Figure 17 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Write down the equation which links energy (E), power (P) and time (t).
answer: energy = power × time, or E = P × t

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: A nuclear power station has a power output of 500 MW. Calculate the energy output in 3600 s. Give your answer in J.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Radioactive waste produced by nuclear power stations has a long half-life.

Suggest one precaution taken to reduce the hazard caused by radioactive waste from power stations.
answer: Any one of: bury it; put it in cooling ponds; transport it in secure vessels; store it in metal containers; cover it in concrete

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
Nuclear power stations do not generate electricity every day of the year. One nuclear power station generated electricity for 92% of a year.

one year = 365 days

Calculate the number of days during the year that the nuclear power station generated electricity.
answer: 335.8 days — 92 ÷ 100 × 365. 335 and 336 are accepted.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
A student investigated how the length of a wire affects the resistance of the wire at constant temperature. Figure 18 shows the circuit used: a cell, an ammeter, and a length of resistance wire laid along a metre rule with two crocodile clips on it, with a voltmeter across the clipped section.

The student plotted a graph of resistance against the length of wire.

Describe a method the student could have used to collect the data needed to plot the graph.
answer: Level-marked out of 6. Measure the length of wire between the crocodile clips with the ruler; vary the length by moving the clips; measure the current with the ammeter and the potential difference with the voltmeter; record both for each length; use V = IR to calculate the resistance for each length. Also: repeat and take means, remove anomalies, keep the current low so the wire does not heat up, and disconnect the circuit between readings.
examiner_note: Figure 18 is artwork in the PDF; what it shows is stated in the question.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html: Which graph shows the relationship between the resistance of a wire at constant temperature and its length? Tick one box.
answer: The straight line through the origin — resistance is directly proportional to length
examiner_note: The graphs to choose between are artwork in the PDF. The mark scheme prints the answer as a straight line from the origin, resistance against length.

subject: Physics
name: Paper 1 — June 2024
html:
The student used a cell that had a potential difference of 1.50 V.

Explain why the cell was not an electrical hazard to the student in the investigation.
answer: The potential difference is very low, so there is no risk of an electric shock (and the wire will not get hot enough to burn)
